matching alarms fire on the controllers / virtual controllers they
name. The alarm sweep (backend/alarmwatch) polls the union of every

on the alarm_subscription row.

fields.description:
Cell is a named grouping of equipment inside one site — RC1, GTP2,
the MHE cell holding a pallet wrapper and a pallet labeler.

A site is a flat bag of controllers, virtual controllers and cameras;
a floor is not. The cell is what lets a question be asked of one part
of an installation: what is RC2 running, which cameras cover it, what
is open against it.

Anchoring mirrors Incident: SiteID is required and never rebound, and
OrganizationID is derived from the site at create time. The cell is a
grouping inside a site, not a new tenancy boundary — visibility is the
site's, so backend/access needs no rules of its own for cells.

Membership is many-to-many and lives in cell_controller /
cell_virtual_controller / cell_camera: a camera routinely covers more
than one cell, and a controller can serve two. A cell holding none of
them is valid and expected — the MHE cell has only cameras. The member
ids below are read back from those tables rather than stored on the
row, the way Site.Channels is read back from site_channel.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: cell

fields.description: Controller is the row after its organization and site were updated together.

fields.description:
Group is an organization-owned named bundle of sites that replaces
the direct user<->site relationship: users join groups (user_group),
a group carries a set of sites (group_site) and a set of roles
(group_role) that apply at every one of its sites (the uniform group
model). A user's effective site memberships and per-site permission
grants are the union across every group they belong to.

Cross-org reach follows the old user_site rule shifted one level: a
group may contain a site of another organization only when the
group's owning organization is flagged administrator (Mujin staff
groups sitting on customer sites). Users can only join groups of
their own organization.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: group

fields.description:
VirtualController is a tenant-managed Mujin Controller running as a
container in a per-org namespace inside the portal's own k8s
cluster. (A cross-cluster mode exists for operators who want VC
workloads on physically-separate hardware; in either case the
portal interacts only through the apiserver, so the rest of this
doc applies unchanged.)

Unlike Controller, which represents a physical host that phones home
over the SSH/yamux hub, a VirtualController is provisioned by the
portal itself: the row is created at the same moment the k8s
manifests are applied, and lifecycle (create / pause / resize /
destroy) flows in one direction — portal → k8s. A VirtualController
is reached from the browser through a per-instance subdomain
`<id>-virtual.<baseDomain>` served by the portal binary; the cluster
is never directly addressable.

VirtualController and Controller share zero schema; do not join them
or treat them as discriminated subtypes of a common parent. They
happen to be UI-adjacent in the dashboard, nothing more.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: virtualController

The registry cannot answer it. The discovery sweep skips a
controller it cannot reach — so a transient failure does not wipe
a site's inventory — which means the cameras of a controller that
has since gone down keep the status they had while it was up and
read as online indefinitely. Every byte path dials the
controller, so a camera is only usable when both are true.

fields.description:
Cell is a named grouping of equipment inside one site — RC1, GTP2,
the MHE cell holding a pallet wrapper and a pallet labeler.

A site is a flat bag of controllers, virtual controllers and cameras;
a floor is not. The cell is what lets a question be asked of one part
of an installation: what is RC2 running, which cameras cover it, what
is open against it.

Anchoring mirrors Incident: SiteID is required and never rebound, and
OrganizationID is derived from the site at create time. The cell is a
grouping inside a site, not a new tenancy boundary — visibility is the
site's, so backend/access needs no rules of its own for cells.

Membership is many-to-many and lives in cell_controller /
cell_virtual_controller / cell_camera: a camera routinely covers more
than one cell, and a controller can serve two. A cell holding none of
them is valid and expected — the MHE cell has only cameras. The member
ids below are read back from those tables rather than stored on the
row, the way Site.Channels is read back from site_channel.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: cell

fields.description:

controller list and detail pages — e.g. the physical

fields.description:
HypervisorState is the most recent typed status snapshot the
controller's hypervisord uploaded via
POST /api/v1/controller/reportHypervisorState. The shape mirrors
hypervisor/models.Status (see backend/util/hypervisor); the
portal parses the incoming JSON best-effort so a controller
running a newer hypervisord schema does not drop reports during

as a typed object so the frontend never has to JSON.parse a
string blob.
fields.name: hypervisorState

fields.description:
IsBackupEnabled is the per-controller master switch for the
portal-driven backup path. When true, /api/v1/controller/info
advertises Backup.IsEnabled=true to the controller-side webstack
scheduler, which then pushes archives at BackupIntervalSeconds.
Default false so a fresh deployment is silent until an operator
opts in via SetControllerBackupSettings. Output-only on the
GraphQL surface: ModifyController never touches it; the
dedicated mutation owns input-side validation of the
enabled/interval pair.
fields.name: isBackupEnabled

fields.description:
IsExcludedFromSiteViews leaves this controller's alarms, orchestrators,

The controller stays listed at its site, and its own pages are unchanged.
See docs/decisions/20261106-exclude-controller-from-site-views.md.
fields.name: isExcludedFromSiteViews

fields.description:
IsSyncEnabled is the per-controller master switch for the
portal-driven data-sync path. When true, /api/v1/controller/info
advertises Sync.IsEnabled=true to the controller-side webstack
synchronizer, which then auto-discovers this portal and pushes
live state at the synchronizer's own cadence. Default false so a
fresh deployment is silent until an operator opts in via
SetControllerSyncSettings. Output-only on the GraphQL surface;
the dedicated mutation owns input-side validation.
fields.name: isSyncEnabled

fields.description:
OrganizationID is the organization this controller belongs to.
Empty means unassigned — only administrator organizations can

(ApproveControllerLink) and released by an org admin via

fields.description:
Region is the home region for this controller. It is fixed at
provisioning time and immutable once set: a controller phoning

one-shot backfill under backend/cmd/regionbackfill/ stamps every

fields.description:
ReleaseID is the catalog Release the controller's running
container maps to. Set by the release linker
(backend/release.LinkController) off HypervisorState.Docker
labels; empty when no release row matched. Output-only — there
is no user-facing "set release" mutation; the linker is the
only writer.

ReleaseImageID being nil while ReleaseID is set indicates a
version-only match: the controller's image VERSION resolved
onto this release, but its HEAD/PRESET labels did not match
any registered ReleaseImage row (operator built a local patch
on top of the release, or has not uploaded the matching image
metadata yet).
fields.name: releaseId

fields.description:
ReleaseImageID is the specific ReleaseImage row whose HEAD +
PRESET docker labels matched the controller's running image.
Non-nil only when ReleaseID is also set; together they signal

fields.description:

the target site is in the controller's own org.

fields.description:
SyncIntervalSeconds is the push cadence the portal dictates for the
controller's sync peer, in seconds, surfaced on Sync.intervalSeconds in
the controller-info response. Zero means the portal does not dictate a

fields.description:

fields.description:

GetUsername returns DefaultControllerUsername when the pointer
is nil OR the dereferenced string is empty, so callers never
need to repeat the fallback themselves. Output-only on the
GraphQL surface: it is readable, but it is set together with the

fields.description:

fields.description:
IsStrictRunMode reports whether the master restarts anything in the
active run mode and refuses to start anything outside it. Worth
showing because it explains why an orchestrator is not running.
fields.name: isStrictRunMode

fields.description:
ObservedAt is when the controller was actually snapshotted. The
ordering key for a consumer applying transitions: a frame older
than one already applied is stale, which is what makes reconnecting
onto a pod with a slightly behind cache entry safe.
fields.name: observedAt

fields.description: Orchestrators are the running orchestrators, sorted by id.
fields.name: orchestrators

fields.description: Source is the path that served the query.
fields.name: source

fields.description:
StatusMessage is the master's status line. Carries real diagnostic
text -- on controller1174 it reported a robotbridges command
timeout alongside the run mode.
fields.name: statusMessage

fields.description: AlarmMessage describes the failure.
fields.name: alarmMessage

fields.description:
ResourceTypes names the progress rows this alarm concerns, as
SyncResourceType values. Empty for an alarm about the push as a whole,
or when the controller does not name them.
fields.name: resourceTypes

fields.description:
ChangedAt is when this row's counts last changed, on the portal clock,
so a row that stalls while others move can be told apart. Null when
not known.
fields.name: changedAt

fields.description: PushedCount is how many backlog rows have been pushed in this run.
fields.name: pushedCount

fields.description:
ResourceType is a SyncResourceType value, or a type name from a newer
controller that this portal does not know.
fields.name: resourceType

fields.description:
TotalCount is the run's backlog as the controller last counted it,
null while the controller is still counting it. Only the stat entry
total can grow within a run. The row is done once PushedCount reaches
this value, so a zero is an empty backlog.
fields.name: totalCount

fields.description:
ReportIntervalSeconds is how often the controller reports while it
pushes, which is as often as polling this is worth.
fields.name: reportIntervalSeconds

fields.description:
RetrievedAt is when the portal answered. The report's timestamps are
on the portal clock too, so a consumer measures their age against
this rather than against its own clock.
fields.name: retrievedAt

fields.description:
SyncState is the controller's latest sync report. Null when the
controller has not reported since its sync settings last changed.
fields.name: syncState

fields.description: Synced is how much of the controller's data the portal holds.
fields.name: synced

fields.description:
Alarms lists every current failure of the push, whatever its kind. Any
entry means the push reported a failure.
fields.name: alarms

fields.description:
Progress has one row per resource type the controller pushes, covering
the first backlog push only. Empty while the controller has not started
pushing.
fields.name: progress

fields.description: ReportedAt is when the portal received the report, on the portal clock.
fields.name: reportedAt

fields.description:
RunStartedAt is when the portal received the first report of the
current push run, on the portal clock. The controller starts a new run
after a sync policy change or a restart.
fields.name: runStartedAt

fields.description:
ArrivedCount is how many of this type's rows reached the portal since
the current run started, as of Count, at most the run's reported
total. Null when the type was not counted that way.
fields.name: arrivedCount

fields.description:
Count is how many rows the portal held for this controller when last
counted, at most a few minutes before RetrievedAt. It can exceed what
the controller still has, since controllers delete their own history.
fields.name: count

fields.description:
CountChangedAt is when the portal last saw this type's count change,
on the portal clock. Null when not known.
fields.name: countChangedAt

fields.description:
EstimatedFinalCount estimates how many rows the portal will hold once
the current push run finishes. Null when the latest report has no
backlog count for this type.
fields.name: estimatedFinalCount

fields.description:
EstimatedHeldCount estimates how many rows the portal holds now. Its
ratio to EstimatedFinalCount is the progress. Null when the latest
report has no backlog count for this type.
fields.name: estimatedHeldCount

fields.description:
NewRowShare is the share, between 0 and 1, of the rows the current run
pushes that the portal did not already hold. It is 1 until measured,
so a run that re-pushes rows the portal already holds reads low at
first.
fields.name: newRowShare

fields.description:
ResourceType is a SyncResourceType value, carried as a string so a
type added later still comes through.
fields.name: resourceType

fields.description:
IsAvailable is false when the portal could not count its data.
Resources is then empty and means unknown, not zero.
fields.name: isAvailable

fields.description:
Resources has one entry per counted resource type, in a stable
order. Empty when IsAvailable is false.
fields.name: resources

fields.description: ControllerID is the counted controller.
fields.name: controllerId

fields.description: Count is how many of the controller's users the portal holds.
fields.name: count

fields.description:
IsAvailable is false when the portal could not count. Count is then
zero and means unknown.
fields.name: isAvailable

fields.description: Buckets are the per-interval rows, ascending by StartedAt.
fields.name: buckets

fields.description: EndedAt is the exclusive window end.
fields.name: endedAt

fields.description: IntervalType echoes the requested bucket size.
fields.name: intervalType

fields.description:
RetrievedAt is when the controller was actually queried — read
it together with the cache TTL to judge staleness.
fields.name: retrievedAt

fields.description:
Source is the path that served the query (live / cloud /
virtual) so consumers can label staleness.
fields.name: source

fields.description: StartedAt is the inclusive window start.
fields.name: startedAt

fields.description:
Totals pre-aggregates the window so simple consumers (cards,
agent tools) do not re-implement the throughput formulas.
fields.name: totals

fields.description:
HumanInterventionCount is the number of human interventions
(numberOfHumanInterventions).
fields.name: humanInterventionCount

fields.description:
OrderCycleFinishStatuses counts finished order cycles by status,
with the webstack-assigned outcome category.
fields.name: orderCycleFinishStatuses

fields.description:
PickOperationCount is the number of pick operations
(systemThroughput.numberOfPickOperations).
fields.name: pickOperationCount

fields.description:
PickedPartCount is the number of parts picked
(systemThroughput.numberOfPickedParts).
fields.name: pickedPartCount

fields.description:
RobotBusySeconds is the summed robot cycle time for the bucket
(directRobotThroughput.sum).
fields.name: robotBusySeconds

fields.description:
RobotCycleCount is the direct-robot-throughput sample count for
the bucket (directRobotThroughput.totalCount).
fields.name: robotCycleCount

fields.description:
RobotOrigins splits those two by the orchestrator that ran the cycles.
Parts/hour for any sub-range adds each origin's own
count * 3600 / busy seconds, because they work in parallel: pooling them
would give the pace of an average robot, not of the line.
fields.name: robotOrigins

fields.description: StartedAt is the bucket start.
fields.name: startedAt

fields.description:
StateDurations breaks down production-cycle wall-clock time by
state for the bucket.
fields.name: stateDurations

fields.description: Category is webstack's outcome classification of the status.
fields.name: category

fields.description: Count of order cycles finished with this status.
fields.name: count

fields.description:
OrderCycleFinishStatus is the order-cycle finish status (e.g.
FinishedOrderComplete, FinishedNoMoreTargetsNotEmpty). Webstack
still calls this a finish code on the wire.
fields.name: orderCycleFinishStatus

fields.description: OriginID tells origins apart within a controller's statistics.
fields.name: originId

fields.description:
RobotCycleCount and RobotBusySeconds are this origin's share of the
bucket's.
fields.name: robotCycleCount

fields.description:
SampleCount is the aggregator's per-row count — an aggregation
detail, NOT a cycle count; use Seconds for duration.
fields.name: sampleCount

fields.description: Seconds is wall-clock time in the state (stateDurations[].sum).
fields.name: seconds

fields.description:
State is the production-cycle state name (e.g. Running, Paused,
PausedOnError, Stopped). Free-form — owned by the controller.
fields.name: state

fields.description:
ActiveAlarmCount is the number of currently-open Error and Critical alarms,
counted server-side on the controller (no alarm rows move for
the badge).
fields.name: activeAlarmCount

fields.description: ControllerID is set when the target is a physical controller.
fields.name: controllerId

fields.description:
IsAvailable is false when the target's webstack could not be
reached; the data fields are zero-valued then.
fields.name: isAvailable

fields.description: RetrievedAt is when the target was actually queried (cache-aware).
fields.name: retrievedAt

fields.description:
Source is the path that served the data (live / cloud /
virtual). Cloud data lags the controller.
fields.name: source

fields.description: StartedAt is the rollup window start (start of the local day).
fields.name: startedAt

fields.description: Totals carries today's aggregated statistics.
fields.name: totals

fields.description:
VirtualControllerID is set when the target is a virtual
controller.
fields.name: virtualControllerId

fields.description: AverageCycleSeconds is the mean robot cycle time over the window.
fields.name: averageCycleSeconds

fields.description:
DirectRobotThroughputPartsPerHour adds each origin's pace over the
window (totalCount*3600/sum; bin-width independent), assuming robots
and manual stations work at the same time.
fields.name: directRobotThroughputPartsPerHour

fields.description:
ErrorRate is HumanInterventionCount over PickedPartCount — human
interventions per pick (0 when nothing was picked in the window).
fields.name: errorRate

fields.description: HumanInterventionCount sums human interventions over the window.
fields.name: humanInterventionCount

fields.description:
OrderCycleFinishStatuses rolls finish-status counts up over the
window, descending by Count.
fields.name: orderCycleFinishStatuses

fields.description: PickOperationCount sums pick operations over the window.
fields.name: pickOperationCount

fields.description: PickedPartCount sums picked parts over the window.
fields.name: pickedPartCount

fields.description:
RunningRatio is Running seconds over total covered seconds
(0 when no production-cycle entries exist in the window).
fields.name: runningRatio

fields.description:
StateDurations rolls production-cycle state time up over the
window, descending by Seconds.
fields.name: stateDurations

fields.description:
SucceededCount / FailedCount / InterruptedCount sum finished
order cycles by outcome category over the window.
fields.name: succeededCount

fields.description:
ListMeta is the shared pagination metadata every List* return value
carries under `meta`. TotalCount is the number of rows matching the
query's filters *before* First/After are applied, so the table can
render a real page count.
fields.name: meta

fields.description:
ControllerComment is the controller's free-form admin note,
supplied so the usage-history page can label rows without a
second round-trip. Empty on the dashboard ListControllerUsages
path, which does not populate it.
fields.name: controllerComment

fields.description: ID of the Controller
fields.name: controllerId

fields.description: EndedAt is the end of the summed bucket (exclusive).
fields.name: endedAt

fields.description:
IntervalType matches the requested bucket (e.g. "minute",
"hour"). See util/timeutils for the set of values.
fields.name: intervalType

fields.description: Received is bytes received by the portal from the controller in the bucket.
fields.name: received

fields.description: Sent is bytes sent from the portal to the controller in the bucket.
fields.name: sent

fields.description: StartedAt is the start of the summed bucket.
fields.name: startedAt

fields.description: Up is seconds the controller was attached during the bucket.
fields.name: up

fields.description:
IconURL is a path on the Portal host that serves the app's icon image
(PNG or SVG) to a caller holding Portal's token. Null when the app has
no icon.
fields.name: iconUrl

fields.description: Name is the app's display name.
fields.name: name

fields.description:
OpenPath is the path under the controller's web UI host that shows
the app, for example /app/<baseRoute>. Join it to the host that
matches the list's source (live, cloud or virtual); opening it
through a web session handoff lands signed in.
fields.name: openPath

fields.description: VersionString is the app's version, empty when the manifest has none.
fields.name: versionString

fields.description: WebAppID is the app's stable id on the controller.
fields.name: webAppId

fields.description:
IsAvailable is false when no webstack could be reached: the
controller is offline with no synced copy, or a virtual controller
has no running webstack. WebApps is then empty.
fields.name: isAvailable

fields.description:
Source is the path that served the list: live, or cloud for a
controller that is offline. The web UI to open an app in is the one
on the same path. Null when IsAvailable is false.
fields.name: source

fields.description: WebApps are the installed apps that can be opened, sorted by name.
fields.name: webApps

fields.description:
Run lock. Set while a runner pod is actively turning the
conversation; cleared on graceful end. ActiveRunHeartbeatAt
is bumped every few seconds; a stale heartbeat (>30s) lets
another pod claim the lock and run integrity recovery.
ActiveRunRegion identifies which regional Redis carries the
runner's pub/sub channels — see docs/subsystems/ai.md "Per-region
Redis".
fields.name: activeRunId

fields.description:
ArchivedAt is the soft-delete marker the /agent landing
filters by. Set via ArchiveConversation; cleared by passing
archived=false. Archived rows stay in the table (transcript,
sub-agent links, summarizer output preserved) but drop off
the "recent" view.
fields.name: archivedAt

fields.description:
Chat is a room where people talk, and the assistant too when someone
addresses it. What is said is stored once, as ChatMessage rows; each member
has a conversation of kind chat that points here and holds only what is
private to them. OrganizationID is the customer organization of the
members, or the administrator organization when every member is a Mujin
user. There is no administrator reach into a chat: it is read by its
members and nobody else.
fields.name: chat

fields.description:
ConversationKind says whether this is the person's thread with the
assistant or their side of a chat with people. ChatID names the chat for
the latter; Chat is the room as the reader sees it, filled by the list
and get reads. A conversation of kind chat is read by its owner only:
no administrator reaches it.
fields.name: conversationKind

fields.description:
HasRunningBackgroundWork says background work the conversation started is
queued or running, so a list can mark it without a query per row.
fields.name: hasRunningBackgroundWork

fields.description:
IsMain says this is the person's main chat with the assistant: the one
conversation the chat box opens on and the assistant's own messages
land in. There is one per person and organization. It is never archived,
renamed or deleted, and clients show it as "Main chat".
fields.name: isMain

fields.description:
IsTitleCustom is true once a person renamed the conversation; the
summarizer then leaves the title alone.
fields.name: isTitleCustom

fields.description:
LastMessageAt mirrors the timestamp of the most recent
ConversationMessage row. The summarizer's inactivity gate
reads this without scanning the messages table.
fields.name: lastMessageAt

fields.description:
LastMessageExcerpt is the start of the last thing said in a conversation
with the assistant, for the one line under its title in the list. Chats
carry theirs on the chat. Set by a list that asks for it.
fields.name: lastMessageExcerpt

fields.description:
LastProviderID snapshots the provider used on the most recent
turn. Updated by the runner when a turn completes; surfaces in
the UI so reopening an old conversation pre-selects the right
provider.
fields.name: lastProviderId

fields.description:
ParentConversationID names the parent conversation when this
row is a child sub-agent thread spawned via the agent tool.
Nil for top-level user conversations. The agent tool reuses a
child by (parent_conversation_id, agent_id, purpose) so a
multi-turn agent-to-agent dialog persists across tool calls.
fields.name: parentConversationId

fields.description:
Purpose is the free-form key the calling agent supplies when
it spawns or reuses a child conversation. Together with
parent_conversation_id and agent_id it identifies the child
thread; empty string is a valid value.
fields.name: purpose

fields.description:
Summarizer claim. Same lease pattern as the run lock; aging
out lets another pod retry if a previous attempt died mid-call.
fields.name: summarizerInstanceId

fields.description:
Title and Summary are filled by the background summarizer once
the conversation has been idle for a few minutes. SummarizedAt
is the lease/age marker; modified_at > summarized_at means
re-summarize is due.
fields.name: title

fields.description:
ExpiresAt is when the approval stops being valid, 10 minutes after it
was requested.
fields.name: expiresAt

fields.description:
Preview is the one-line description of the call the approval card
shows.
fields.name: preview

fields.description:
Chat carries the event of a chat the conversation belongs to, when Type
starts with chat_. Its Type repeats this one's.
fields.name: chat

fields.description:
ConversationUpdated is published when the conversation's own row changes in
a way a client shows without reading it again. Today that is the title: the
placeholder cut from the first message, the summarizer's title a few seconds
after the first turn, and a rename. ConversationTitle is the title now
stored; IsTitleCustom says the person typed it, so no summary will replace it.

It belongs to no run (its event has no RunID) and is never replayed to a
client that connects later, which reads the title with the conversation.
fields.name: conversationUpdated

fields.description:
ConversationModelSwitch is published once when a turn that started on the
quick model moves to the main model, so the client can show "Thinking
harder" while the larger model reads. FromModelRole and ToModelRole are
"quick" and "main". SwitchCause is "tool" (the quick model called
think_harder) or "judgment" (the effort judgment found the message needs a
closer look). ProviderID and ModelName name the model now answering.
SwitchReason is a few words on why, empty for a judgment. IsReasoningEffortRaised
says the main model also runs with raised reasoning effort.
fields.name: modelSwitch

fields.description:
ConversationPendingApproval is published when an interactive run reaches
a write, destructive or outward tool call that the user has not allowed to
run without asking. The frontend surfaces an allow once / always allow this
kind / deny affordance; resolution flows through the resolveToolApproval
mutation, which writes the row and publishes the regional Redis
notification the runner pod's broker is waiting on.

Risk is one of write, destructive or outward. Preview is the one-line
description of the call. ExpiresAt is when the approval stops being valid:
resolving it later is refused and the call fails.
fields.name: pendingApproval

fields.description:
ConversationReacted is published when a reaction on a message changes: the
emoji now there from that reactor, or an empty Emoji when the reactor took
theirs away. ReactorKind is "user" or "assistant"; ReactorUserID names the
person and is empty for the assistant.

It belongs to no run (its event has no RunID) and is never replayed to a
client that connects later, which reads reactions with the messages.
fields.name: reacted

fields.description:
ConversationRoundRetry is published when a round's stream failed in transit
and the round starts over: the client drops the partial text it streamed
under DiscardedMessageID.
fields.name: roundRetry

fields.description:
ConversationRunComplete ends a run. StopReason is end_turn for an answer,
cancelled for a stop, and round_limit or repeated_failure for a turn the
runner ended itself; TurnEndReason is the sentence the person is shown for
those, and is empty for an ordinary answer.
fields.name: runComplete

fields.description:
ConversationRunError ends a run that failed. Error is the error text for
operators and job records; TurnEndReason is the bounded sentence the person
is shown ("The model provider is unavailable"), the same one stored as the
turn's end note.
fields.name: runError

fields.description:
ConversationTextDelta and the sibling Conversation* variant types
each correspond to one ConversationEvent.Type literal.
fields.name: textDelta

fields.description:
ThreadRootMessageID is the thread the run is answering in, on every event
of such a run. A client showing the main history leaves it out.
fields.name: threadRootMessageId

fields.description:
ConversationToolResult carries a finished call. ToolNote is the one short
line the tool wrote about the call ("3 controllers"), safe to show with tool
display off; DurationMS is how long the tool ran, without any wait for an
approval.
fields.name: toolResult

fields.description: Call is the call a chat message is the line of, with empty content.
fields.name: call

fields.description:
Content is the message body — string, []ContentPart, or any
JSON shape the providers package serializes. Consumers should
route through providers.ChatMessage.UnmarshalJSON to pick the
right shape.
fields.name: content

fields.description:
The fields below are set on a message of a chat conversation that is
shared with the chat's members (IsChatMessage), as opposed to the
reader's own rows with the assistant. AuthorUserID is the person who said
it, empty for the assistant, which speaks for OnBehalfOfUserID. Names are
as the reader sees them: a member of another organization carries that
organization's name.
fields.name: isChatMessage

fields.description:
LinkPreviewsRemovedAt is when the sender removed the previews of the
message's links.
fields.name: linkPreviewsRemovedAt

fields.description: Mentions are the names the sender chose from the list in a chat message.
fields.name: mentions

fields.description:
Metadata holds turn-specific extras: stop_reason qualifiers,
{"cancelled": true, "cause": ...}, etc. Free-form JSON. On a
context_summary row it carries {"summary": true,
"resumeFromMessageId": "...", "coverageRecorded": bool} — see
agents.persistSummaryMessage.
fields.name: metadata

fields.description:
Reactions are the emoji put on the message, oldest first. They are
loaded only by reads that ask for them (db.ConversationMessageOptions
ShouldIncludeReactions).
fields.name: reactions

fields.description:
ReplyToExcerpt and ReplyToAuthorName quote the message replied to, and
are empty when it was said before the reader joined. In a conversation
with the assistant the server stores them when the message is sent,
read from the message replied to and never from what the client sent.
fields.name: replyToExcerpt

fields.description:
ThreadReplyCount and ThreadLastReplyAt describe the thread hanging from
this message, and are empty when it has none.
fields.name: threadReplyCount

fields.description:
ThreadRootMessageID is the message whose thread this one is in, empty for
a message of the main history. Every row of an assistant's answer in a
thread carries it, its tool calls too.
fields.name: threadRootMessageId

fields.description:
ToolCallID and ToolName are only set on `tool` role messages
— they pair this row with the matching ToolCalls[i] entry on
the prior assistant message.
fields.name: toolCallId

fields.description:
ToolCalls is the assistant's tool-call array (only set on
assistant messages). Wire-format is providers.[]ToolCall.
fields.name: toolCalls

fields.description:
Usage captures per-turn token counts (only set on assistant
messages). Wire-format is providers.UsageInformation.
fields.name: usage

fields.description:
ViewingKind, ViewingID and ViewingLabel name the page the person had
open when they sent the message (a conversationviewing kind, the
resource id, and the label the server resolved). Set only on user
messages sent with a page the sender could see.
fields.name: viewingKind

fields.description: VoiceMessage is set on a voice message of a chat, which has no text.
fields.name: voiceMessage

fields.description:
IsAcknowledgment marks the reaction the server added for the assistant
when a message arrived, as opposed to one the assistant chose with the
conversation tool. The model is not shown the former.
fields.name: isAcknowledgment

fields.description:
ReactorUserID is the person who reacted; empty for the assistant, and
for a person whose account is gone.
fields.name: reactorUserId

fields.description:
ReasonKind names what ended the turn (see turnEndReasonKind*) so a
client words it in the person's language; ReasonParameters holds the
values that wording needs.
fields.name: reasonKind

fields.description: PromptText is the question, or the one-line preview of the call to approve.
fields.name: promptText

fields.description: ToolName and ToolRisk are set for an approval only.
fields.name: toolName

fields.description: TargetsAnswered is how many targets returned a response.
fields.name: targetsAnswered

fields.description: TargetsRequested is how many were asked.
fields.name: targetsRequested

fields.description:
Agent is a globally-owned (admin-org-admin-managed) prompt entry. An agent
bundles a system prompt and model choices; every run of it gets every tool
the assistant has. Customer organizations are granted use of an agent via
OrganizationAgent rows.

Agents are not tied to a single Provider — DefaultProviderID is
merely the picker's initial selection, and the user (or the
per-turn providerId argument on sendMessage) can override.
fields.name: agent

fields.description:
Cell is a named grouping of equipment inside one site — RC1, GTP2,
the MHE cell holding a pallet wrapper and a pallet labeler.

A site is a flat bag of controllers, virtual controllers and cameras;
a floor is not. The cell is what lets a question be asked of one part
of an installation: what is RC2 running, which cameras cover it, what
is open against it.

Anchoring mirrors Incident: SiteID is required and never rebound, and
OrganizationID is derived from the site at create time. The cell is a
grouping inside a site, not a new tenancy boundary — visibility is the
site's, so backend/access needs no rules of its own for cells.

Membership is many-to-many and lives in cell_controller /
cell_virtual_controller / cell_camera: a camera routinely covers more
than one cell, and a controller can serve two. A cell holding none of
them is valid and expected — the MHE cell has only cameras. The member
ids below are read back from those tables rather than stored on the
row, the way Site.Channels is read back from site_channel.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: cell

fields.description:
Conversation is a per-(organization, user, agent) chat thread.
The user owns the conversation; the agent provides the system
prompt and tool allow-list. LastProviderID snapshots the most
recently used Provider so the UI can resume with the same picker
state, but every turn can override via the providerId argument
on sendMessage.

Run-lock and summarizer-claim columns hold the cross-pod
coordination state described in docs/subsystems/ai.md "Stateless across
portal instances": ActiveRun* says which pod is currently running
the conversation and which regional Redis carries its pub/sub
channels; Summarizer* says which pod is generating title/summary.
Both follow the conditional-UPDATE-as-lease pattern.
fields.name: conversation

fields.description:
ConversationTodo is a per-conversation task item. Lives in its own table
(not on ConversationMessage) because todos outlive any single
message and have their own lifecycle. Org/user are denormalized
for cheap visibility filtering.
fields.name: todo

fields.description:
Chat is a room where people talk, and the assistant too when someone
addresses it. What is said is stored once, as ChatMessage rows; each member
has a conversation of kind chat that points here and holds only what is
private to them. OrganizationID is the customer organization of the
members, or the administrator organization when every member is a Mujin
user. There is no administrator reach into a chat: it is read by its
members and nobody else.
fields.name: chat

fields.description:
Conversation is a per-(organization, user, agent) chat thread.
The user owns the conversation; the agent provides the system
prompt and tool allow-list. LastProviderID snapshots the most
recently used Provider so the UI can resume with the same picker
state, but every turn can override via the providerId argument
on sendMessage.

Run-lock and summarizer-claim columns hold the cross-pod
coordination state described in docs/subsystems/ai.md "Stateless across
portal instances": ActiveRun* says which pod is currently running
the conversation and which regional Redis carries its pub/sub
channels; Summarizer* says which pod is generating title/summary.
Both follow the conditional-UPDATE-as-lease pattern.
fields.name: conversation

fields.description:
Group is an organization-owned named bundle of sites that replaces
the direct user<->site relationship: users join groups (user_group),
a group carries a set of sites (group_site) and a set of roles
(group_role) that apply at every one of its sites (the uniform group
model). A user's effective site memberships and per-site permission
grants are the union across every group they belong to.

Cross-org reach follows the old user_site rule shifted one level: a
group may contain a site of another organization only when the
group's owning organization is flagged administrator (Mujin staff
groups sitting on customer sites). Users can only join groups of
their own organization.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: group

fields.description:
Job is a per-(organization, user) scheduled work item. The

fields.description:
Page is a wiki-style documentation node attached to a Site. Pages
form a tree (ParentPageID; nil at the root); each page carries a
title and a markdown content stream. Customers see contracts,
drawings, manuals, runbooks, and incident reports through this
surface.

Permissions:
  - read: holders of site:read at the page's site (admin-org
    cross-org admins always)
  - write: gated by the page verbs (page:edit/publish/move/delete/
    revert) bound through a role, or a cross-organization
    administrator — see access.CanEditPages.

Content lives in PageRevision (immutable, append-only) — Page does
not store title or content directly. Reads join through
CurrentRevisionID to surface the latest revision; history reads
enumerate PageRevision in reverse-chronological order. The
CurrentRevisionID is nullable so the table can be created before
any CreatePage transaction populates it.

row; Page.CurrentRevisionID flips to the new row. Attachments

the page id) so historical revisions keep their attachment set
even after later edits remove the references.

GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.

configuration. The same ProviderType may appear multiple times with
different keys, base URLs, or model names — Name is the
human-readable disambiguator. APIKeyCiphertext stores the AES-GCM
sealed key derived via HKDF from the portal's master secret-file;
see util/secretbox. The plaintext key is never returned over the
wire — UIs render APIKeyFingerprint instead.

Customer organizations gain access via OrganizationProvider rows;
without a grant a non-admin caller does not see this provider in
listAuthorizedProviders.

fields.description:
Release is one entry in the portal's release catalog — a versioned
build of an application (today only "appcontroller") that operators
publish for customers to track against. Controllers report their
running container's docker labels via the hypervisor state push,
and the release linker (backend/release) matches the VERSION/HEAD
labels onto a Release + ReleaseImage row so the dashboard can show
"this controller is running 0.45.0+mts (exact)" or
"0.45.0+mts (version-matched, HEAD differs)".

Releases are portal-global catalog data:

  - There is no OrganizationID. The admin organization owns every
    row on behalf of the whole portal; CreatedByUserID identifies
    which administrator made the catalog edit.
  - Read visibility is governed by Channel + Site.Channels (see the
    Channel field below). The channel is derived from the version's
    "+..." build suffix; custom builds for a specific customer carry
    their own suffix (and therefore channel) and never leak to other
    tenants.
  - Create / modify / delete is gated by
    platform administrators (platform:administer)
    only. (The same gate apigraph/link.go uses for the link/unlink
    flow.)

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: release

fields.description:
Role is a named bundle of permissions that an organization owns and
binds to a group via group_role; the role's verbs then fire for every
member of that group across the group's sites. A role may carry both
site-scoped verbs (controller/ticket/page/… actions) and org- or
platform-scoped verbs (user/role/organization management,
platform:administer). Org- and platform-scoped operations resolve
through those verbs on the caller's snapshot — see
backend/access/permission.go for the resolution order.

Owner / Operator / Viewer are seeded per organization at create
time so a fresh tenant has working defaults; nothing distinguishes
them from custom roles at the schema level — DeleteRole refuses to
remove a role that still has active (user, site) bindings, which
is the same safety check that protects any in-use custom role.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: role

fields.description:
SSHKey is one customer-owned SSH public key. The row is minted at
"add SSH key" time on the portal frontend; the customer pastes a
public key (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…` form) and the portal stores only
the public half — there is no portal-side keypair generation, no
private material stored, no preshared key. Authorized_keys-style.

Authentication on the inbound :20022 SSH listener: a bare key
(i.e. not an *ssh.Certificate) presented at handshake time is
looked up by raw bytes against this table; a hit means "user X
is connecting" and the post-auth path enforces org-level access
to the controllers / virtual controllers the user wants to
port-forward to. Cert offers signed by the controller CA take
the existing controller branch and never reach this table.

Postgres is the global source of truth across regions. Unlike
WireGuardPeer there is no in-memory cache and no Redis pub/sub:
SSH connect rate is low enough that a per-connect indexed
SELECT on (public_key) is cheap, and a Create / Revoke is
visible to the next inbound connection without any propagation
step.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: sshKey

fields.description:
Site is a sub-organization grouping that scopes which controllers a
non-admin org member can see. Sites belong to a single organization;
a controller is in at most one site (which must be in the
controller's own org); a user can join many sites within their
organization. There is no role distinction inside a site for now —
membership is the whole permission.

Visibility is enforced in backend/access:
  - admin-org members see everything
  - per-user org admins see every controller in their own org
  - regular org members see a controller only when both the
    controller has a site AND they are a member of that site

Site mutations and controller<->site assignments require the per-user
org admin flag, mirroring the link/unlink semantics in apigraph/link.go
(admin-org membership is intentionally not special-cased there).

fields.description:

shown beneath the ticket detail; the order is by

plaintext editor and a WYSIWYG editor and serializes both down to
markdown.

visible only to members of an administrator organization (Mujin
support staff); they are stripped from reads served to regular
org members. Setting IsInternal=true is similarly gated to
admin-org callers — a customer org member cannot mark their own
comment as internal, since "internal" means staff-side.

mode resolved at startup, reported by SystemInfo.ticketConversationMutable:
mutable unless an immutable support desk is declared. When append-only,
removal is a gated, audited redaction. The original request (the first
comment, flagged IsOriginalRequest) follows the same rule.

fields.description:
VirtualController is a tenant-managed Mujin Controller running as a
container in a per-org namespace inside the portal's own k8s
cluster. (A cross-cluster mode exists for operators who want VC
workloads on physically-separate hardware; in either case the
portal interacts only through the apiserver, so the rest of this
doc applies unchanged.)

Unlike Controller, which represents a physical host that phones home
over the SSH/yamux hub, a VirtualController is provisioned by the
portal itself: the row is created at the same moment the k8s
manifests are applied, and lifecycle (create / pause / resize /
destroy) flows in one direction — portal → k8s. A VirtualController
is reached from the browser through a per-instance subdomain
`<id>-virtual.<baseDomain>` served by the portal binary; the cluster
is never directly addressable.

VirtualController and Controller share zero schema; do not join them
or treat them as discriminated subtypes of a common parent. They
happen to be UI-adjacent in the dashboard, nothing more.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.

fields.description:
VirtualControllerSnapshot is a point-in-time capture of a
VirtualController's two PVCs (data + private), backed by k8s
VolumeSnapshot resources. Snapshots are taken under
pause-snapshot-resume so the on-disk state is application-consistent.

Restore is in-place only in v1: the live PVCs are destroyed and
recreated from the snapshot's VolumeSnapshot data sources, so the VC
keeps its id, subdomain, and credentials. The snapshot row itself is
preserved across a restore so the same point-in-time can be rolled
back to again later.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.

fields.description:
WireGuardPeer is one customer-owned WireGuard device. The row is
minted at "add device" time on the portal frontend; the customer
installs the returned wg-quick config on the device and then dials
the regional WG endpoint over UDP to reach controllers and virtual
controllers their organization owns.

The peer's in-tunnel address is derived from the public key, not
stored — `fd00:1:` + the leading 96 bits of `blake2b(public_key)`.
Every pod recomputes the address on demand, so there is no
allocator and no IP column to migrate. Same for controller and
virtual-controller synthetic addresses (`fd00:c::/32`,
`fd00:d::/32`); see WIREGUARD_PLAN.md.

Postgres is the global source of truth across regions; per-region
Redis carries `wireguard:peers:event` notifications for in-region
pods to apply changes inline. Cross-region propagation rides on the
30 s reconcile loop in backend/wg.

The private key is **never** persisted server-side. It is generated
on the request goroutine that mints the device, embedded in the
returned wg-quick config, and dropped from memory once the response
is flushed. The pubkey + preshared key in this row are sufficient
for the portal to authenticate handshakes and decrypt session
keys; reissuing a device is a revoke + remint cycle.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.

fields.description:
Incident is one thing that went wrong at a site — today, a failure a
camera watcher detected and its adjudicator confirmed.

An incident is always anchored to a site: unlike a ticket it has no
organization-level case, because it is by definition something that
happened at an installation. The controller is optional, because it
is resolved by correlating the incident's time range against a
controller's order cycle and that correlation can fail.

Fields divide into two ownership groups, which is what makes a
detector re-push safe. Kind, Confidence and the timestamps are
machine-owned and refreshed on every push.
Title, Description, Status, and the review fields are human-owned and
frozen once ReviewedAt is set — a re-adjudication after review
records an event rather than reverting the reviewer.

Evidence is not modelled here. Clips, frames, and the debug archive
are ordinary Attachment rows linked through attachment_link with a
role; clips and frames hang off the IncidentCamera they came from.

fields.description:
OrganizationAgent authorizes a customer organization to use a
global Agent. The pair (OrganizationID, AgentID) is the composite
primary key — duplicate grants are idempotent. Created only by an
admin-org admin via grantOrganizationAgent; revoked the same way.

The grant is observed on every list call
(listAuthorizedAgents), on every createConversation authorization
check (the chosen Agent must be granted to the caller's org), and
on every execute action against an existing conversation —
sendMessage, answerQuestion, and resolveToolApproval all
revalidate the grant before advancing the run (see
requireConversationAgentExecuteAccess). Revoking a grant therefore
stops all further AI work, on both new and already-open
conversations; the org keeps only read-only visibility into past
conversations (issue #37, CWE-863).

fields.description:
OrganizationProvider authorizes a customer organization to use a
global Provider. The pair (OrganizationID, ProviderID) is the
composite primary key — duplicate grants are idempotent. Created
only by an admin-org admin via grantOrganizationProvider; revoked
the same way.

The grant is observed on every list call (listAuthorizedProviders)
and on every sendMessage authorization check (the chosen Provider
must be granted to the caller's org). Revoking a grant immediately
hides the provider from new sends, but does not retroactively
scrub historical ConversationMessage rows referencing the provider.

fields.description:

Machine-owned: the detector reports it, because the detector is
what can see the floor. Orthogonal to Status — see IncidentActivityStatus.
fields.name: activityStatus

fields.description:
ActivityStatusSetByUser is who last set the activity by hand.

Set means a person overrode the detector, and the detector stops
owning the field: somebody standing on the floor knows better than
a camera, and a push must not undo them. Nil means nobody has, and
every push refreshes it as before.
fields.name: activityStatusSetByUserId

fields.description:
CellID names the cell within SiteID the incident happened at —
RC2 rather than the whole Carlisle floor. Optional, and a
narrowing of the site rather than an alternative to it: the
resolver requires the cell to belong to SiteID, so every
site-scoped access check stays correct without reading this
field.

Separate from ControllerID because the two answer different
questions and either can be known without the other: the MHE cell
has no controller to correlate, and a correlated controller can
serve two cells.
fields.name: cellId

fields.description:
CellIDSetByUser is who last set the cell by hand.

Set means a person overrode the detector, and the detector stops
owning the field: somebody standing on the floor knows which cell
it was, and a re-push must not undo them. Nil means nobody has,
and every push refreshes it as before. Same rule as
ActivityStatusSetByUser.
fields.name: cellIdSetByUserId

fields.description: ClearedAt is when the detector last observed the condition gone.
fields.name: clearedAt

fields.description:
Confidence is the detector's confidence in the range 0..1. Nil
for a manually-opened incident.

fields.description:
ControllerID is the controller correlated to this incident, when
the correlation succeeded.

fields.description:

Description caches above were minted from.

fields.description:

floor has settled. A detector asking for logs as it reports wants
the window after the event, not the instant it opened. Nil means
claim as soon as the sweep sees it, which is what a person
pressing collect gets.

fields.description:
Debug-collection state. At most one collection per incident, so
it lives here rather than in a job table.

fields.description:
DetectedAt is when the detector decided, which trails StartedAt
by however long adjudication took.
fields.name: detectedAt

fields.description:
ExternalReference is the detector's own id for this incident. Unique
per (source, site) so a retried push updates rather than
duplicates, and so two sites' detectors cannot collide.
fields.name: externalReference

fields.description:

"DropTargetFailure". Free-form so a detector can add classes
without a portal migration.

fields.description:
OrganizationID is derived from the site at create time and never
changes.

fields.description:
PreviewAttachmentID is the still a list card shows for this
incident — the primary angle's clean frame. Resolved rather than
stored: it is derivable from the evidence, and a stored copy would
go stale the moment a re-push refined which angle is primary.

fields.description:
Status is the review lifecycle. Server-managed: it moves through
the Transition path, not a raw field write.

fields.description:
SiteID is the installation this happened at. Required, set at
create time, never rebound.
fields.name: siteId

fields.description:
Source names the detector that reported this incident, as it
names itself. Empty means a person opened it in the portal.
Deliberately free-form: the portal has no business hardcoding
the name of any particular detector, and a second one must not
need a migration.

fields.description:
StartedAt and EndedAt bound what happened. They drive camera
playback and the debug-log collection window.

fields.description:
ViewerCapabilities is request-scoped: the site verbs the calling
user holds at this incident's site. Never persisted.
fields.name: viewerCapabilities

fields.description:
CameraID references the camera registry row. Nil when the sweep has
never seen this camera — see the type comment.

fields.description:
CameraName is the display name as it read at detection time. A
caller shows the registry's current name and falls back to this.
fields.name: cameraName

fields.description:
ClipStartedAt is the wall-clock time of the first frame of this
angle's clip. Without it the angles cannot be lined up: each
detector export starts whenever that camera's footage starts, so
two clips of the same event routinely begin seconds apart, and
DetectionBox.AtMilliseconds is clip-relative only. With it the
player derives each angle's offset from the earliest clip and
plays every angle on one playhead.

Nil for an angle with no clip, and for anything a detector pushed
before it started reporting the value — such an angle plays
standalone rather than joining the synchronized wall.
fields.name: clipStartedAt

fields.description:
ControllerID is the controller whose NVR owns this camera. It may
differ from the incident's correlated controller — the camera
watching a cell is not necessarily attached to that cell.
fields.name: controllerId

fields.description:

from this table, and are request-scoped rather than persisted.
Both are empty for an angle with no registry row, and TimeZone is
also empty when the NVR reported no zone — a caller falls back to
CameraName and to the reader's own labelled zone.
fields.name: currentName

fields.description:
IsPrimary marks the angle the detector judged best — the one the
UI opens first.
fields.name: isPrimary

fields.description:
OriginCameraID is the identifier the camera came from — the NVR's
own — which is what the live playback routes take.
fields.name: originCameraId

fields.description:
TimeZone is what lets an incident's clips and times render on the
floor's clock instead of the reader's.
fields.name: timeZone

fields.description:
AttachmentID names the clip or still the boxes are drawn against,
so the frontend knows which media to overlay. Empty means the
camera's primary clip.
fields.name: attachmentId

fields.description:
Boxes is the track: one entry per instant the detector had a
position for this object, ordered by AtMilliseconds.
fields.name: boxes

fields.description: Confidence is the detector's confidence in 0..1.

fields.description:
IncidentCameraID is the angle this was seen from. The boxes are
in that camera's frame of reference.

fields.description:
IsPrimary marks the object that caused the incident, as opposed
to context objects that give the rule its reference points.
fields.name: isPrimary

fields.description: Kind is the detected class, e.g. "box" or "pallet".
fields.name: kind

fields.description:
Label is the human-readable description of what the detector
believes this object is doing — the sentence a reviewer reads
next to the box.
fields.name: label

fields.description:
TrackID is the detector's own identifier for this object across
frames. Kept so a dispute can be correlated back to the
detector's own logs.
fields.name: trackId

fields.description:
ActorUserID is the user who triggered the event. Null for events
a detector or a background sweep produced.
fields.name: actorUserId

fields.description:
FromValue is the previous value when the event records a
transition. Empty for add-only events.
fields.name: fromValue

fields.description: IncidentID is the parent incident. Set at create time, never null.
fields.name: incidentId

fields.description: Kind is the discriminator — see IncidentEventKind constants.
fields.name: kind

fields.description:
OrganizationID and SiteID denormalize the parent's anchors so
per-org and per-site reads do not need to join through incident.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
ToValue is the new value, or the added/removed entity id for
add/remove events. Empty when the event has no payload.
fields.name: toValue

fields.description:
Bucket is the start of the period — midnight, or the top of the
hour, in whichever zone the count was asked for.
fields.name: bucket

fields.description: LinkedByUserID is null for a detector-created link.
fields.name: linkedByUserId

fields.description: RelatedIncidentID is the other end of the link.
fields.name: relatedIncidentId

fields.description:
Source names the detector that drew the link, as it names
itself. A human edit clears it, which is what stops a later
detector push from undoing the correction.

fields.description:
Incident is one thing that went wrong at a site — today, a failure a
camera watcher detected and its adjudicator confirmed.

An incident is always anchored to a site: unlike a ticket it has no
organization-level case, because it is by definition something that
happened at an installation. The controller is optional, because it
is resolved by correlating the incident's time range against a
controller's order cycle and that correlation can fail.

Fields divide into two ownership groups, which is what makes a
detector re-push safe. Kind, Confidence and the timestamps are
machine-owned and refreshed on every push.
Title, Description, Status, and the review fields are human-owned and
frozen once ReviewedAt is set — a re-adjudication after review
records an event rather than reverting the reviewer.

Evidence is not modelled here. Clips, frames, and the debug archive
are ordinary Attachment rows linked through attachment_link with a
role; clips and frames hang off the IncidentCamera they came from.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: incident

fields.description:
AuthorUserID is the user who triggered the write. Null when a
detector produced the revision, which is exactly how a reader
tells machine wording from human wording.
fields.name: authorUserId

fields.description: CreatedAt is the revision's creation time, immutable.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description: IncidentID is the parent incident. Set at create time, never null.
fields.name: incidentId

fields.description:
OrganizationID and SiteID denormalize the parent's anchors so
per-org and per-site reads do not join through incident.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
RevisionNumber is the per-incident monotonic counter (1, 2, 3, …).
Allocated inside the write transaction; the unique
(incident_id, revision_number) index backs the allocation.
fields.name: revisionNumber

fields.description:
Source names the detector that produced this revision, as it
names itself; empty means a person wrote it. Redundant with a
null AuthorUserID today, but explicit so a second detector is
distinguishable rather than merely anonymous.
fields.name: source

fields.description:
Summary is an optional commit-message style label. The detector
path uses it to record why it rewrote the text — an initial push
versus a re-adjudication reads very differently to a reviewer.
fields.name: summary

fields.description:
Title and Description are the values at the time this revision
was minted. Description is markdown only, no HTML.
fields.name: title

fields.description: IsEnabled toggles the subscription without deleting it.
fields.name: isEnabled

fields.description:
MinimumConfidence is a detector-confidence floor in 0..1. A site
that produces a lot of low-confidence detections can be watched
for only the ones worth interrupting someone over. Nil or 0 means
every incident notifies.
fields.name: minimumConfidence

fields.description:
OrganizationID denormalizes the owner's organization so the
notify path can scope its work without joining through user.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description: SiteID is the site being watched.
fields.name: siteId

fields.description:
UserID is the owning recipient. Every subscription belongs to
exactly one user; the inbox rows it produces are theirs.
fields.name: userId

fields.description:
IncidentSubscription is one user's standing request to be told when
incidents happen at a site.

Site-scoped rather than per-controller (the shape alarm
subscriptions use) because an incident is anchored to a site and its
controller correlation is optional — subscribing per controller would
silently miss every incident the detector could not correlate.

The subscription only names who wants to hear; whether they actually
receive an email is the notification preference layer's call, and
visibility is re-checked at send time so a user who lost access to
the site stops being told about it.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: incidentSubscription

fields.description:
Agent is a globally-owned (admin-org-admin-managed) prompt entry. An agent
bundles a system prompt and model choices; every run of it gets every tool
the assistant has. Customer organizations are granted use of an agent via
OrganizationAgent rows.

Agents are not tied to a single Provider — DefaultProviderID is
merely the picker's initial selection, and the user (or the
per-turn providerId argument on sendMessage) can override.
fields.name: agent

fields.description:
Cell is a named grouping of equipment inside one site — RC1, GTP2,
the MHE cell holding a pallet wrapper and a pallet labeler.

A site is a flat bag of controllers, virtual controllers and cameras;
a floor is not. The cell is what lets a question be asked of one part
of an installation: what is RC2 running, which cameras cover it, what
is open against it.

Anchoring mirrors Incident: SiteID is required and never rebound, and
OrganizationID is derived from the site at create time. The cell is a
grouping inside a site, not a new tenancy boundary — visibility is the
site's, so backend/access needs no rules of its own for cells.

Membership is many-to-many and lives in cell_controller /
cell_virtual_controller / cell_camera: a camera routinely covers more
than one cell, and a controller can serve two. A cell holding none of
them is valid and expected — the MHE cell has only cameras. The member
ids below are read back from those tables rather than stored on the
row, the way Site.Channels is read back from site_channel.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: cell

fields.description:
ConversationTodo is a per-conversation task item. Lives in its own table
(not on ConversationMessage) because todos outlive any single
message and have their own lifecycle. Org/user are denormalized
for cheap visibility filtering.
fields.name: todo

fields.description:
EmailTemplate is one entry in the portal's email template catalog —
the operator-editable source for one kind of outbound mail (the
sign-in email, the ticket-assigned notification, …). Templates are
portal-global catalog data, mirroring Release:

  - There is no OrganizationID. One row per Kind serves the whole
    portal. The sign-in email in particular is rendered before any
    organization context exists, so a global row is the only shape
    that fits every send path.
  - Create / modify is gated on the email_template:manage platform verb
    — admin-org admins only, the same gate the Release catalog uses.
    ModifiedByUserID identifies which administrator made the edit.
  - The catalog is seeded at boot from the templates embedded in
    util/mailers (the canonical English defaults); an admin edit
    overrides the seeded copy in place. The embedded copy remains
    the render-time fallback if a row is somehow missing.

From / Subject / Text / HTML are localized: callers send a list of
(locale, text) entries and the mailer renders the entry matching
the requesting locale (English fallback via LookupLocalizedString).
Storing all four as localized lists preserves the per-language
shape the embedded emails/<locale>/<kind>.{from,subject,text,html}
tree already had.

Each entry's Text is a Go text/template (subject, from, plaintext
body) or html/template (HTML body) source string — the same action
syntax ({{.name}}, {{.code}}, …) the embedded files use, minus the
{{define}} wrapper.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: emailTemplate

fields.description:
Group is an organization-owned named bundle of sites that replaces
the direct user<->site relationship: users join groups (user_group),
a group carries a set of sites (group_site) and a set of roles
(group_role) that apply at every one of its sites (the uniform group
model). A user's effective site memberships and per-site permission
grants are the union across every group they belong to.

Cross-org reach follows the old user_site rule shifted one level: a
group may contain a site of another organization only when the
group's owning organization is flagged administrator (Mujin staff
groups sitting on customer sites). Users can only join groups of
their own organization.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: group

fields.description:
Job is a per-(organization, user) scheduled work item. The
scheduler fires it on a recurring or one-shot trigger by appending a
user message to PinnedConversationID and invoking the runner.

See docs/jobs.md (forthcoming) for the multi-instance scheduler
design — claim transitions ride conditional UPDATEs on the row,
mirroring the summarizer-claim pattern already in use elsewhere in
agents/.

Visibility is per-(organization, user); in-org admins do not see
another user's jobs (same rationale as Conversation / memory pages /
ConversationTodo).
fields.name: job

fields.description:
Notification is one entry in a user's inbox. Exactly one of the
polymorphic subject columns (TicketID today; PageID/ConversationID
reserved for future kinds) is populated per row — the Kind picks
which one the frontend should follow on click. Notifications are
scoped to a single recipient; if two users are mentioned in the
same ticket they get two separate rows, so the read-state per user
is naturally independent.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: notification

fields.description:
OAuthClient is a relying party registered against the portal's
OpenID Connect provider — a first-party Mujin app (controller
webstack, uicore, Grafana, internal tool) that offers "Login with
Mujin Portal". The provider lives in api/apioidc; this model is the
registry an administrator manages through the OAuthClient GraphQL
surface.

ID is the internal ULID primary key; ClientID is the public,
stable identifier the relying party presents at /authorize and
/token — the two are deliberately distinct so the wire-facing id
can be rotated independently of the row.

All fields except ID are pointers. Generated Update() and GetXxx()
methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: oauthClient

fields.description:
Page is a wiki-style documentation node attached to a Site. Pages
form a tree (ParentPageID; nil at the root); each page carries a
title and a markdown content stream. Customers see contracts,
drawings, manuals, runbooks, and incident reports through this
surface.

Permissions:
  - read: holders of site:read at the page's site (admin-org
    cross-org admins always)
  - write: gated by the page verbs (page:edit/publish/move/delete/
    revert) bound through a role, or a cross-organization
    administrator — see access.CanEditPages.

Content lives in PageRevision (immutable, append-only) — Page does
not store title or content directly. Reads join through
CurrentRevisionID to surface the latest revision; history reads
enumerate PageRevision in reverse-chronological order. The
CurrentRevisionID is nullable so the table can be created before
any CreatePage transaction populates it.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: page

fields.description:
Passkey is one WebAuthn credential registered by a user as their
second authentication factor. The row is minted when the user
completes a registration ceremony on the passkeys settings page;
only the credential's public half is stored. A user with at least
one passkey must pass an assertion ceremony after the first factor
(magic link / OTP / SSO) before their session is authorized.

Deletion is hard: removing the row (owner, or an org administrator
recovering a locked-out member) immediately drops the user back to
email-only login. The audit_event trail records create and delete.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: passkey

fields.description:
Provider is a globally-owned (admin-org-admin-managed) LLM API
configuration. The same ProviderType may appear multiple times with
different keys, base URLs, or model names — Name is the
human-readable disambiguator. APIKeyCiphertext stores the AES-GCM
sealed key derived via HKDF from the portal's master secret-file;
see util/secretbox. The plaintext key is never returned over the
wire — UIs render APIKeyFingerprint instead.

Customer organizations gain access via OrganizationProvider rows;
without a grant a non-admin caller does not see this provider in
listAuthorizedProviders.
fields.name: provider

fields.description:
Release is one entry in the portal's release catalog — a versioned
build of an application (today only "appcontroller") that operators
publish for customers to track against. Controllers report their
running container's docker labels via the hypervisor state push,
and the release linker (backend/release) matches the VERSION/HEAD
labels onto a Release + ReleaseImage row so the dashboard can show
"this controller is running 0.45.0+mts (exact)" or
"0.45.0+mts (version-matched, HEAD differs)".

Releases are portal-global catalog data:

  - There is no OrganizationID. The admin organization owns every
    row on behalf of the whole portal; CreatedByUserID identifies
    which administrator made the catalog edit.
  - Read visibility is governed by Channel + Site.Channels (see the
    Channel field below). The channel is derived from the version's
    "+..." build suffix; custom builds for a specific customer carry
    their own suffix (and therefore channel) and never leak to other
    tenants.
  - Create / modify / delete is gated by
    platform administrators (platform:administer)
    only. (The same gate apigraph/link.go uses for the link/unlink
    flow.)

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: release

fields.description:
Role is a named bundle of permissions that an organization owns and
binds to a group via group_role; the role's verbs then fire for every
member of that group across the group's sites. A role may carry both
site-scoped verbs (controller/ticket/page/… actions) and org- or
platform-scoped verbs (user/role/organization management,
platform:administer). Org- and platform-scoped operations resolve
through those verbs on the caller's snapshot — see
backend/access/permission.go for the resolution order.

Owner / Operator / Viewer are seeded per organization at create
time so a fresh tenant has working defaults; nothing distinguishes
them from custom roles at the schema level — DeleteRole refuses to
remove a role that still has active (user, site) bindings, which
is the same safety check that protects any in-use custom role.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: role

fields.description:
SSHKey is one customer-owned SSH public key. The row is minted at
"add SSH key" time on the portal frontend; the customer pastes a
public key (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…` form) and the portal stores only
the public half — there is no portal-side keypair generation, no
private material stored, no preshared key. Authorized_keys-style.

Authentication on the inbound :20022 SSH listener: a bare key
(i.e. not an *ssh.Certificate) presented at handshake time is
looked up by raw bytes against this table; a hit means "user X
is connecting" and the post-auth path enforces org-level access
to the controllers / virtual controllers the user wants to
port-forward to. Cert offers signed by the controller CA take
the existing controller branch and never reach this table.

Postgres is the global source of truth across regions. Unlike
WireGuardPeer there is no in-memory cache and no Redis pub/sub:
SSH connect rate is low enough that a per-connect indexed
SELECT on (public_key) is cheap, and a Create / Revoke is
visible to the next inbound connection without any propagation
step.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: sshKey

fields.description:
Site is a sub-organization grouping that scopes which controllers a
non-admin org member can see. Sites belong to a single organization;
a controller is in at most one site (which must be in the
controller's own org); a user can join many sites within their
organization. There is no role distinction inside a site for now —
membership is the whole permission.

Visibility is enforced in backend/access:
  - admin-org members see everything
  - per-user org admins see every controller in their own org
  - regular org members see a controller only when both the
    controller has a site AND they are a member of that site

Site mutations and controller<->site assignments require the per-user
org admin flag, mirroring the link/unlink semantics in apigraph/link.go
(admin-org membership is intentionally not special-cased there).

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: site

fields.description:
TicketComment is a reply on a Ticket. Comments form the conversation
shown beneath the ticket detail; the order is by
CreatedAt ascending. Comments are markdown-only on the wire (same
convention as Ticket.Description); the frontend offers both a
plaintext editor and a WYSIWYG editor and serializes both down to
markdown.

Comments support a soft IsInternal flag. Internal comments are
visible only to members of an administrator organization (Mujin
support staff); they are stripped from reads served to regular
org members. Setting IsInternal=true is similarly gated to
admin-org callers — a customer org member cannot mark their own
comment as internal, since "internal" means staff-side.

Edit (a revision) and delete (a soft delete) follow the conversation
mode resolved at startup, reported by SystemInfo.ticketConversationMutable:
mutable unless an immutable support desk is declared. When append-only,
removal is a gated, audited redaction. The original request (the first
comment, flagged IsOriginalRequest) follows the same rule.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: ticketComment

fields.description:
Ticket is a customer support request belonging to a single
organization. The portal is the source of truth — there is no sync
to an external ticketing system in this version (Zendesk/GitLab
mirrors, if added later, will live in a separate package and write
to a side table rather than reshape this model).

Ticket follows the VirtualController pattern: pointer fields so
partial-update semantics fall out of nil-vs-non-nil; the row is the
source of truth; soft state (assignees, controllers) lives in
many-to-many join tables; comments and attachments are separate
models linked back by ticket_id.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: ticket

fields.description:
Token is the updated row; never includes the bearer value (the
modify path cannot recover the secret).
fields.name: token
