fields.description:
VirtualController is a tenant-managed Mujin Controller running as a
container in a per-org namespace inside the portal's own k8s
cluster. (A cross-cluster mode exists for operators who want VC
workloads on physically-separate hardware; in either case the
portal interacts only through the apiserver, so the rest of this
doc applies unchanged.)

Unlike Controller, which represents a physical host that phones home
over the SSH/yamux hub, a VirtualController is provisioned by the
portal itself: the row is created at the same moment the k8s
manifests are applied, and lifecycle (create / pause / resize /
destroy) flows in one direction — portal → k8s. A VirtualController
is reached from the browser through a per-instance subdomain
`<id>-virtual.<baseDomain>` served by the portal binary; the cluster
is never directly addressable.

VirtualController and Controller share zero schema; do not join them
or treat them as discriminated subtypes of a common parent. They
happen to be UI-adjacent in the dashboard, nothing more.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: virtualController

fields.description:
VirtualControllerSnapshot is a point-in-time capture of a
VirtualController's two PVCs (data + private), backed by k8s
VolumeSnapshot resources. Snapshots are taken under
pause-snapshot-resume so the on-disk state is application-consistent.

Restore is in-place only in v1: the live PVCs are destroyed and
recreated from the snapshot's VolumeSnapshot data sources, so the VC
keeps its id, subdomain, and credentials. The snapshot row itself is
preserved across a restore so the same point-in-time can be rolled
back to again later.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: virtualControllerSnapshot

fields.description:
WireGuardPeer is one customer-owned WireGuard device. The row is
minted at "add device" time on the portal frontend; the customer
installs the returned wg-quick config on the device and then dials
the regional WG endpoint over UDP to reach controllers and virtual
controllers their organization owns.

The peer's in-tunnel address is derived from the public key, not
stored — `fd00:1:` + the leading 96 bits of `blake2b(public_key)`.
Every pod recomputes the address on demand, so there is no
allocator and no IP column to migrate. Same for controller and
virtual-controller synthetic addresses (`fd00:c::/32`,
`fd00:d::/32`); see WIREGUARD_PLAN.md.

Postgres is the global source of truth across regions; per-region
Redis carries `wireguard:peers:event` notifications for in-region
pods to apply changes inline. Cross-region propagation rides on the
30 s reconcile loop in backend/wg.

The private key is **never** persisted server-side. It is generated
on the request goroutine that mints the device, embedded in the
returned wg-quick config, and dropped from memory once the response
is flushed. The pubkey + preshared key in this row are sufficient
for the portal to authenticate handshakes and decrypt session
keys; reissuing a device is a revoke + remint cycle.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: wireGuardPeer

fields.description:
ActorUserID is the user who triggered the notification (the
assigner, the mention author). Nil for system-generated kinds.
fields.name: actorUserId

fields.description:
AgentGoalID and AgentGoalWaitID are the subject of an agent_goal_needs_you
row: the goal and the wait it is in. AgentGoalWaitID is the idempotency
key. AgentGoalTitle and AgentGoalQuestion snapshot the goal's title and
what it needs from the person. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: agentGoalId

fields.description:
AgentJobID and AgentJobRunID are the subject of an agent_job_failed row:
the job and the run that failed. AgentJobRunID is the idempotency key.
AgentJobName and AgentJobFailureMessage snapshot the job's name and why
the run failed; IsAgentJobPaused says the failure paused the job. Nil for
other kinds.
fields.name: agentJobId

fields.description:
AgentMessageID is the subject of an agent_message row: the speak-first
turn, which is also the idempotency key. AgentMessageConversationID is
where the assistant spoke, AgentMessageReason why, and AgentMessageExcerpt
the start of what it said. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: agentMessageId

fields.description:
AgentWaitingID is the subject of an agent_waiting row: the question or
approval card, which is also the idempotency key. AgentWaitingKind says
which of the two it is, AgentWaitingConversationID where it is waiting, and
AgentWaitingPrompt and AgentWaitingToolName what it asked and which tool
wants to run. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: agentWaitingId

fields.description:
AlarmLevel / AlarmStatus / AlarmMessage snapshot the alarm at
notify time. Alarms are never stored in the portal (they are
proxied live from each controller's webstack), so without the
snapshot the inbox could not render an alarm that has since
cleared. AlarmLevel is the controller's free-form level string
(e.g. "Critical"), AlarmStatus the alarm code, AlarmMessage the
human-readable text. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: alarmLevel

fields.description:
AlarmLogEntryID is the controller's stable per-occurrence id for
the alarm. It is the idempotency subject for an alarm row —
re-polling the same active alarm yields the same id, so the row
is written once. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: alarmLogEntryId

fields.description:
AlarmOriginKind / AlarmOriginLabel snapshot what inside the machine
raised the alarm: the origin's concrete type (e.g. RobotBridgeModule)
and its most specific identifier (robot / device / service name).
Without them the inbox could only say which controller alarmed, not
which component — too generic to act on. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: alarmOriginKind

fields.description:
ChatConversationID is the reader's own conversation of the chat, where
the row links to. Not stored: filled by the notification list, and by the
chat service for the push of a new row.
fields.name: chatConversationId

fields.description:
ChatID and ChatMessageID are the subject of a chat_message row: the chat
and the message. ChatMessageID is the idempotency key. ChatName,
ChatAuthorName and ChatMessageExcerpt snapshot how the message looked
when it was said. Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: chatId

fields.description:
Controller / VirtualController are the resolved subject rows for
an alarm, populated by the resolver so the frontend can render the
machine name + link without a per-row follow-up query.
Not persisted. Nil when the referenced machine no longer exists,
is not visible to the recipient, or the kind has no such subject.
fields.name: controller

fields.description:
ControllerID / VirtualControllerID are the subject for an alarm.
Exactly one is set per row (the alarm fired on a physical or a
virtual controller). Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: controllerId

fields.description:
Incident is the resolved subject row for an incident
notification, populated by the resolver and never persisted. Nil
when the incident is gone or the recipient may no longer read it,
which is what keeps the inbox from naming something they lost
access to.
fields.name: incident

fields.description:
IncidentID is the subject for an incident notification, and its

LinkedTicket is the surviving ticket a closed_as_duplicate event names,
resolved only for a caller who can see it, so the inbox can say where
the conversation went. Not persisted.

fields.description:
OrganizationID denormalizes the recipient's owning org so
per-org admin reads do not need to join through user.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
OrganizationName / SiteName are the resolved org and site display
names of the notification's subject — the alarm's machine or the
ticket — populated by the resolver from the already-loaded,
access-gated subject row (not snapshotted, so they reflect the
current names). Not persisted. Nil when the subject is gone / not
visible, or for a subject with no site.
fields.name: organizationName

fields.description:
OriginControllerID is the cluster member that actually raised the
alarm when it was aggregated by a cluster head (controller or
virtual controller); empty/nil when raised locally. It is part of
the idempotency key so two members sharing a controller-local
log_entry_id do not collapse into one notification.
fields.name: originControllerId

fields.description:
ReadAt is set when Status flips to read; nil while unread.
Server-managed — clients send Status, not ReadAt.
fields.name: readAt

fields.description:
Status is the only user-mutable field. Transitions unread → read
when the recipient acknowledges it (click-through or explicit
mark-read). ReadAt is stamped at the same time.
fields.name: status

fields.description:
Ticket is the resolved subject row, populated by the resolver
when the notification kind points at a ticket so the frontend
can render the canonical `/ticket/$sequence` link
without a per-row follow-up query. Not persisted. Nil when the
referenced ticket no longer exists or the kind has no ticket
subject.
fields.name: ticket

fields.description:
TicketComment is a reply on a Ticket. Comments form the conversation
shown beneath the ticket detail; the order is by
CreatedAt ascending. Comments are markdown-only on the wire (same
convention as Ticket.Description); the frontend offers both a
plaintext editor and a WYSIWYG editor and serializes both down to
markdown.

Comments support a soft IsInternal flag. Internal comments are
visible only to members of an administrator organization (Mujin
support staff); they are stripped from reads served to regular
org members. Setting IsInternal=true is similarly gated to
admin-org callers — a customer org member cannot mark their own
comment as internal, since "internal" means staff-side.

Edit (a revision) and delete (a soft delete) follow the conversation
mode resolved at startup, reported by SystemInfo.ticketConversationMutable:
mutable unless an immutable support desk is declared. When append-only,
removal is a gated, audited redaction. The original request (the first
comment, flagged IsOriginalRequest) follows the same rule.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: ticketComment

fields.description:
TicketEvent / TicketComment are the resolved subject of a
ticket_lifecycle / ticket_comment row, populated by the resolver so the
inbox can render what actually happened (the event's kind and from/to
values, e.g. status Open → Closed, or the comment body) without a
follow-up query. Not persisted. Nil when the entry is gone / not
visible, or the kind has no such subject. The comment is resolved only
for viewers allowed to see it (internal comments stay admin-only),
mirroring the fan-out gate.
fields.name: ticketEvent

fields.description:
TicketEventID / TicketCommentID are the subject for ticket_lifecycle /
ticket_comment: the specific timeline entry that fired the
notification (the event for ticket_lifecycle, the comment for
ticket_comment). They are also the idempotency subject. Nil for
other kinds.
fields.name: ticketEventId

fields.description:
TicketID is the subject for ticket_assigned and ticket_mentioned.
Nil for other kinds.
fields.name: ticketId

fields.description:
UserID is the recipient. Every read goes through (UserID,
CreatedAt DESC); never null.
fields.name: userId

fields.description:
VirtualController is a tenant-managed Mujin Controller running as a
container in a per-org namespace inside the portal's own k8s
cluster. (A cross-cluster mode exists for operators who want VC
workloads on physically-separate hardware; in either case the
portal interacts only through the apiserver, so the rest of this
doc applies unchanged.)

Unlike Controller, which represents a physical host that phones home
over the SSH/yamux hub, a VirtualController is provisioned by the
portal itself: the row is created at the same moment the k8s
manifests are applied, and lifecycle (create / pause / resize /
destroy) flows in one direction — portal → k8s. A VirtualController
is reached from the browser through a per-instance subdomain
`<id>-virtual.<baseDomain>` served by the portal binary; the cluster
is never directly addressable.

VirtualController and Controller share zero schema; do not join them
or treat them as discriminated subtypes of a common parent. They
happen to be UI-adjacent in the dashboard, nothing more.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.

fields.description:
Chat is a room where people talk, and the assistant too when someone
addresses it. What is said is stored once, as ChatMessage rows; each member
has a conversation of kind chat that points here and holds only what is
private to them. OrganizationID is the customer organization of the
members, or the administrator organization when every member is a Mujin
user. There is no administrator reach into a chat: it is read by its
members and nobody else.
fields.name: chat

fields.description:
Conversation is a per-(organization, user, agent) chat thread.
The user owns the conversation; the agent provides the system
prompt and tool allow-list. LastProviderID snapshots the most
recently used Provider so the UI can resume with the same picker
state, but every turn can override via the providerId argument
on sendMessage.

Run-lock and summarizer-claim columns hold the cross-pod
coordination state described in docs/subsystems/ai.md "Stateless across
portal instances": ActiveRun* says which pod is currently running
the conversation and which regional Redis carries its pub/sub
channels; Summarizer* says which pod is generating title/summary.
Both follow the conditional-UPDATE-as-lease pattern.

fields.description:
ExpiresAt is when the URL stops being treated as fresh. The
frontend uses this to discard a stale tab's URL and re-mint.
fields.name: expiresAt

fields.name: url

fields.description:
AutoReloadAmount is how much each auto-reload top-up charges,
in billing-currency minor units.
fields.name: autoReloadAmount

fields.description:
AutoReloadThreshold is the balance level at or below which
auto-reload fires, in billing-currency minor units.
fields.name: autoReloadThreshold

fields.description:
BillingAlertThreshold is the highest spend-alert checkpoint already
raised this cycle, so the alert sweep does not re-notify a crossed
level. Self-resets when the cycle rolls. Audit/state only.
fields.name: billingAlertThreshold

fields.description:
BillingBalance is the organization's prepaid balance in its
billing-currency minor units. Metered usage beyond the plan's included
allowances (overage) is charged against this balance as it accrues;
when it would run dry, metered actions are blocked unless auto-reload
tops it up. Topped up via the add-funds Checkout and (optionally)
auto-reload; drawn down by the settlement sweep. Output-only — moved
only through the transaction ledger.
fields.name: billingBalance

fields.description:
BillingCurrency is the ISO 4217 code (lowercase, matching Stripe)
this organization is billed in (e.g. "usd", "jpy"). Drives which
PlanPrice the pricing page, cost roll-up, and Checkout use. Empty
defaults to "usd". Stripe locks a customer's currency after its
first invoice, so this is effectively fixed once the org subscribes.
fields.name: billingCurrency

fields.description:
BillingLastAutoReloadAt is when auto-reload last fired an off-session
charge. The settlement sweep refuses to fire another within
autoReloadCooldown of it — a duration-based guard (not a wall-clock
bucket) so a charge cannot double-fire across an hour boundary while
the crediting webhook lags, and a too-small reload amount cannot
re-charge the card faster than the cooldown. Output-only.
fields.name: billingLastAutoReloadAt

fields.description:
BillingSettledOverage is how much of the current cycle's
overage the settlement sweep has already charged against the balance,
anchored to BillingSettlementPeriodStartedAt. The sweep charges only the
delta (current overage minus this) each run; enforcement treats it as
0 when the anchor no longer matches the live period. Output-only.
fields.name: billingSettledOverage

fields.description:
BillingSettlementPeriodEndedAt is the end of the settled window, paired
with BillingSettlementPeriodStartedAt. When the window changes, settlement
compares the new period's start against this end to tell a clean cycle
roll (no overlap → the new overage is new and is charged) from an
overlapping window change such as free→paid (the new Stripe window
starts mid-cycle and overlaps the old calendar one → the overlapping
overage was already charged, so it is carried forward, not
re-charged). Output-only.
fields.name: billingSettlementPeriodEndedAt

fields.description:
BillingSettlementPeriodStartedAt anchors BillingSettledOverage
to a billing cycle; when the live cycle's start differs, the settled
counter is stale and treated as 0 (the new cycle starts fresh).
Output-only.
fields.name: billingSettlementPeriodStartedAt

fields.description:

spend within a billing cycle, in billing-currency minor units. Even
when the prepaid balance (or auto-reload) could cover more, metered
actions are blocked once cycle overage reaches this limit. nil means
no cap (balance is then the only ceiling).
fields.name: spendingLimit

fields.description:
SpendingWarning is a soft warning level below the spending
limit: when cycle overage crosses it the alert sweep notifies the
org's administrators, but nothing is blocked. nil means no custom

fields.name: spendingWarning

fields.description:

fields.description:
StripeCustomerID is the organization's Stripe customer, the single

marginal rate) counts against it; when a user reaches it, that user's
AI turns are blocked even if the org still has balance and headroom
under the org-wide SpendingLimit. nil means no per-user cap. Set by an
org billing manager.
fields.name: userSpendingLimit

fields.description:
WorkOSOrganizationID is the WorkOS organization identifier
(e.g. "org_01HXYZ…") used when SSOProvider == "workos".
fields.name: workosOrganizationId

fields.description:
DecidedAt / DecidedByUserID / DecisionReason record the decision.
The reason is optional and is never shown to the registrant — a
rejection sends no email — so it is a note for other
administrators reading the queue later.
fields.name: decidedAt

fields.description:
Email is the registrant's work address, already proven reachable.
It is the natural key: one live request per address.
fields.name: email

fields.description:
Locale is the interface locale the registrant signed up in. The
approval can land days later, from an administrator with a
different language, so the welcome email reads this rather than
anything about the approver.
fields.name: locale

fields.description:
OrganizationID / UserID name what an approval created. Empty on a
pending or rejected request.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
OrganizationName is the display name the registrant asked for, and
Country the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code fixing the organization's
billing currency. Both are carried verbatim from the sign-up form.
fields.name: organizationName

fields.description: Status is pending until an administrator decides.
fields.name: status

fields.description:
OrganizationRegistration is one self-service sign-up awaiting a
platform administrator's decision, created only when the registrant
proves control of the email address — clicking the magic link or
entering the code. Until then the request lives on the magic-link
Session alone (RegistrationOrganizationName / RegistrationCountry), so
an unauthenticated mutation cannot write rows.

The row exists only when the server runs with
--registration-approval-required. Without the flag the sign-up
provisions its organization the moment the email is proven, exactly as
it did before the gate existed, and no registration is ever recorded.

Approval is what creates the Organization, its Domain, its default
roles and groups, and the registrant as its first administrator —
OrganizationID and UserID are stamped with the result so the row also
serves as the audit trail of what the decision produced.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.

only in the brief window between CreatePage's row insert and

in-progress state. ModifyPage updates these without minting

is display chrome that should not bloat revision history.

IsPublished reports whether the page has at least one

Computed per request so the client shows an affordance only to a

fields.description:
Name is the user-supplied label, e.g. "MacBook Touch ID" or
"YubiKey 5". Free text, editable after registration.
fields.name: name

fields.description:
UsedAt is the most recent successful assertion. Refreshed by the
login flow's finish step; excluded from ModifiedAt bumps.
fields.name: usedAt

fields.description:
UserID is the owning user. A passkey is bound to a single user;
its only use is authorizing that user's login sessions.
fields.name: userId

fields.description:
Job is a per-(organization, user) scheduled work item. The
scheduler fires it on a recurring or one-shot trigger by appending a
user message to PinnedConversationID and invoking the runner.

See docs/jobs.md (forthcoming) for the multi-instance scheduler
design — claim transitions ride conditional UPDATEs on the row,
mirroring the summarizer-claim pattern already in use elsewhere in
agents/.

Visibility is per-(organization, user); in-org admins do not see
another user's jobs (same rationale as Conversation / memory pages /
ConversationTodo).
fields.name: job

fields.description:
AITokenLimits is the plan's set of AI-token hard limits — each a
(scope, interval, limit) rule (e.g. per-user-per-day,
per-organization-per-cycle). Every rule is enforced; an AI turn is
blocked when any rule's usage is reached. Distinct from
IncludedAITokens (the free per-cycle allowance the cost roll-up
bills overage past). Stored as a jsonb list on the plan row.
fields.name: aiTokenLimits

fields.description: BillingInterval is the base-fee recurrence cadence.
fields.name: billingInterval

fields.description: Timestamp when the plan was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
CreatedByUserID is the admin-org administrator who created the
row. Audit only; never used for authz.
fields.name: createdByUserId

fields.description:
DeletedAt is set when DeletePlan lands. Soft delete — the row is
kept so a subscription still resolves its (now-retired) plan for
historical invoices. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows by default.
fields.name: deletedAt

fields.description:
Description is the short marketing one-liner shown beside the
tier on the pricing page. Localized with the same shape as
DisplayName. Optional.
fields.name: description

fields.description:
DisplayName is the human-facing label rendered on the pricing
and billing pages. Localized: one entry per supported locale,
resolved per-viewer with English fallback (LookupLocalizedString).
fields.name: displayName

fields.description:
Included allowances bundled into the base fee. Usage up to these
quantities is free; the cost roll-up only charges the overage.
fields.name: includedAiTokens

fields.description:
IsActive gates whether the plan is offered to new subscribers.
Retiring a tier flips this false; existing subscriptions keep
their plan until they migrate.
fields.name: isActive

fields.description:
IsDefault marks the free/default plan every organization falls
back to when it has no active paid subscription. At most one live
plan should carry it; the billing layer resolves an org's
effective plan as (active subscription's plan) OR this default.
Typically baseFee=0 with modest included allowances.
fields.name: isDefault

fields.description:
IsDocumentationIncluded gates access to the Mujin user manual (the
in-portal product documentation) for subscribers on this plan. A
per-plan capability flag rather than a hardcoded free/paid split, so
the perk can be granted or withheld per tier independently of price.
The frontend hides the manual button when the org's effective plan
has this false.
fields.name: isDocumentationIncluded

fields.description:
MaxConcurrentVirtualControllers caps how many non-destroyed VCs a
subscriber may hold at once — the VC count limit that sits
alongside the running-hours limit. Zero means no count cap.
fields.name: maxConcurrentVirtualControllers

fields.description:
MaxVirtualControllerHours caps total VC running-hours per billing
cycle — a hard ceiling distinct from IncludedVirtualControllerHours
(the free allowance) and from the budget. Once a cycle's running
hours reach this value, starting or keeping VCs running is blocked
even if budget remains. Zero means no hour cap (running-hours are
then bounded only by the budget).
fields.name: maxVirtualControllerHours

fields.description: Timestamp when the plan was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
ModifiedByUserID is the admin-org administrator behind the
latest edit. Audit only.
fields.name: modifiedByUserId

fields.description:
Name is the stable machine identifier for the tier (e.g.
"starter", "growth", "enterprise"). Unique among live rows.
fields.name: name

fields.description:
Prices holds one PlanPrice per offered currency — a global customer
is billed in its own currency's prices, not an FX conversion. The
cost roll-up and Checkout pick the entry matching the org's billing
currency (falling back to the first when unset). Stored as jsonb.
fields.name: prices

fields.description:
SortOrder controls the left-to-right ordering of tiers on the
pricing page. Lower sorts first.
fields.name: sortOrder

fields.description:
StripeProductID is the shared Stripe Product for the tier; the
per-currency Prices live in each PlanPrice below.
fields.name: stripeProductId

fields.description:
AITokenPrices are per-million rates in the currency's minor units, one
per AITokenCategory.
fields.name: aiTokenPrices

fields.description: Currency is lower-case ISO 4217, matching PlanPrice.Currency.
fields.name: currency

fields.description:
ProviderModelName is Provider.ModelName, the provider-specific model
identifier.
fields.name: providerModelName

fields.description:
SpeechRequestPrice is the price of one speech (text-to-speech)
request, in the currency's minor units.
fields.name: speechRequestPrice

fields.description:
AITokenPrices is the per-category AI-token overage price list in this
currency (input / output / cache write / cache read), mirroring the
provider's cost structure. A category absent from the list prices at
zero. Replaces the former single blended per-million rate.
fields.name: aiTokenPrices

fields.description: Currency is the ISO 4217 code (lowercase, matching Stripe).
fields.name: currency

fields.description:
StripeBaseFeePriceID is the Stripe recurring Price for this currency's
base subscription fee — the only Stripe Price the portal provisions
(see billing.EnsurePlanStripeBasePrices) and charges at Checkout. The
shared product lives on the Plan (StripeProductID). Overage on the
metered dimensions above is metered locally and drawn from the prepaid
balance, not invoiced through Stripe, so those lines have no Stripe
Price.
fields.name: stripeBaseFeePriceId

fields.description:
VirtualControllerPrices is the per-size VC running-hour overage
price list in this currency.
fields.name: virtualControllerPrices

inputFields.description:
AITokenPrices is the per-category AI-token overage price list in this
currency (input / output / cache write / cache read), mirroring the
provider's cost structure. A category absent from the list prices at
zero. Replaces the former single blended per-million rate.
inputFields.name: aiTokenPrices

inputFields.description: Currency is the ISO 4217 code (lowercase, matching Stripe).
inputFields.name: currency

inputFields.description:
StripeBaseFeePriceID is the Stripe recurring Price for this currency's
base subscription fee — the only Stripe Price the portal provisions
(see billing.EnsurePlanStripeBasePrices) and charges at Checkout. The
shared product lives on the Plan (StripeProductID). Overage on the
metered dimensions above is metered locally and drawn from the prepaid
balance, not invoiced through Stripe, so those lines have no Stripe
Price.
inputFields.name: stripeBaseFeePriceId

inputFields.description:
VirtualControllerPrices is the per-size VC running-hour overage
price list in this currency.
inputFields.name: virtualControllerPrices

fields.description:
Plan is one tier in the portal's monetization catalog — a fixed
recurring base fee that includes an allowance of metered resources
(AI tokens, virtual-controller running-hours, storage), with
pay-as-you-go overage priced past each allowance.

Plans are portal-global catalog data:

  - There is no OrganizationID. The admin organization owns every
    row on behalf of the whole portal; CreatedByUserID identifies
    which administrator made the catalog edit. An Organization opts
    into a plan through its Subscription row (see subscription.go).
  - Create / modify / delete is gated by
    platform administrators (platform:administer) only,
    the same gate the Release catalog uses. Read of the active
    plan list is open to any authenticated user (the pricing page).
  - Currency amounts are stored as int64 minor units (US cents,
    etc.) and mirrored from the matching Stripe Price on save so the
    real-time, in-portal cost roll-up that drives the hard-block at
    budget needs no synchronous Stripe call on the hot path.

All fields except ID are pointers so partial updates can distinguish
"leave alone" (nil) from "set to the zero value". Generated Update()
and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: plan

fields.description:
ProductionEntryCount is entries whose origins say explicitly that
the cycle was not testing.
fields.name: productionEntryCount

fields.description:
TestingEntryCount is entries whose origins say explicitly that
the cycle was testing. Always excluded.
fields.name: testingEntryCount

fields.description:
UnclassifiedEntryCount is entries whose origins carry no
isTesting flag, or carry both values and so cannot be split. A
mixed-origin entry counts here rather than as production: the
measure is an already-merged total that cannot be split back per
origin, so calling it production would fold testing cycles into a
production number.
fields.name: unclassifiedEntryCount

fields.description:
UnclassifiedIncluded echoes whether the unclassified entries
contributed rows. True in v1, pending a measurement of how large
that share actually is on a real controller.
fields.name: unclassifiedIncluded

fields.description:
ConversationMessage is a single transcript entry. Content,
ToolCalls, Usage, and Metadata are stored as JSON blobs in
`jsonb` columns — the runner's prompt builder unmarshals on
load, the resolvers pass-through to the GraphQL caller as
opaque Data scalars.

Pairing invariant: every assistant message with non-empty
ToolCalls MUST be followed by tool messages whose ToolCallID
covers each call. Recovery (see docs/subsystems/ai.md "Cancelled /
interrupted tool calls") synthesizes [cancelled] tool rows
when a run dies between persisting the assistant message and
persisting the tool results.
fields.name: message

fields.description:
APIKeyFingerprint is a short stable identifier (e.g. the last
four characters of the plaintext key, or a non-reversible
digest of it) suitable for "key …xyz9" UI display. Computed
when the key is set; cleared when the key is cleared.
fields.name: apiKeyFingerprint

fields.description:
BaseURL, when set, overrides the SDK default. Empty means the
vendor's default endpoint. Useful for self-hosted proxies and
OpenAI-compatible third-party gateways.
fields.name: baseUrl

fields.description:
Capabilities advertises optional skills supported by this
configuration. Known values are exported as
ProviderCapability* constants — "chat", "embedding",
"summarizer". The runtime resolves the embedder and summarizer
workers by scanning the catalog for the most recently modified
enabled row carrying the matching capability, so flipping the
bit here is the operator-visible knob (no CLI flag, no pod
restart). Free-form so future singleton-by-class roles can be
added without a schema migration.
fields.name: capabilities

fields.description:
ContextWindow is the model's maximum input+output token budget.
Used by the runner's context-compaction tier thresholds and by
callers that want to size summaries. Operator-supplied; the
portal does not auto-discover model windows.
fields.name: contextWindow

fields.description:
The five prices are nano units (billionths of the currency's main unit)
per million tokens, so $0.075 per million is 75000000. 0 means not
priced: the category costs nothing, except audio input, which is priced
as input. Integers, never floats; see CostNanoUnits.
fields.name: inputPriceNanoUnitsPerMillionTokens

fields.description:
IsEnabled gates whether the provider is selectable. A disabled
provider stays in the catalog (so historical
ConversationMessage rows can dereference its ID) but can no
longer be picked for new turns.
fields.name: isEnabled

fields.description:
MaxOutputTokens caps assistant output per turn. Sent verbatim
to the provider as the max-tokens parameter. Operator-supplied
per Provider so different model rows can reflect different
real provider caps.
fields.name: maxOutputTokens

fields.description:
ModelName is the provider-specific model identifier sent on
every chat request (e.g. "gpt-5.4", "claude-sonnet-4-6").
fields.name: modelName

fields.description:
Name is the human-readable disambiguator shown in admin UIs and
in the user-facing provider picker. Distinct providers of the
same ProviderType MUST have distinct names within the global
catalog (enforced by a unique index in the migration).
fields.name: name

fields.description:
PriceCurrency is the ISO 4217 code the five prices below are in. The
prices are what the vendor charges Mujin for this model, not what a
customer pays: plan prices are separate and unchanged. Staff only, like
every price field; the resolvers clear them for anyone else. Cannot
change once the provider has recorded cost, so one usage bucket never
mixes currencies.
fields.name: priceCurrency

fields.description:
ProviderType selects which client implementation handles this
row. Immutable after create — switching would invalidate stored
model name and any provider-specific tuning.
fields.name: providerType

inputFields.description:
BaseURL, when set, overrides the SDK default. Empty means the
vendor's default endpoint. Useful for self-hosted proxies and
OpenAI-compatible third-party gateways.
inputFields.name: baseUrl

ModelName is the provider-specific model identifier sent on

inputFields.name: modelName

inputFields.description:
Name is the human-readable disambiguator shown in admin UIs and
in the user-facing provider picker. Distinct providers of the
same ProviderType MUST have distinct names within the global

inputFields.name: name

PriceCurrency is the ISO 4217 code the five prices below are in. The
prices are what the vendor charges Mujin for this model, not what a

inputFields.name: priceCurrency

inputFields.description:
ProviderType selects which client implementation handles this
row. Immutable after create — switching would invalidate stored
model name and any provider-specific tuning.
inputFields.name: providerType

fields.description:
SuggestedModelRole is "quick" or "main" when the model name matches a
known pairing, empty otherwise. The agent editor uses it to preselect
the quick and main providers; nothing in the run depends on it.
fields.name: suggestedModelRole

fields.description:
AudioInputTokens are audio tokens a transcription model read. Nothing
reports them yet (see the plan's open questions); the column and the
price exist so the cost is right once something does.
fields.name: audioInputTokens

fields.description:
CostNanoUnits is what the bucket's calls cost at the provider's prices
when they were recorded, in nano units (billionths) of CostCurrency. The
database computes it in AccumulateProviderUsage; a value set by the
caller is ignored. 0 for a bucket recorded before the provider was
priced, until an administrator backfills it.
fields.name: costNanoUnits

fields.description:
Kind tags the kind of LLM call this bucket aggregates so the usage
dashboard can separate user-facing conversation spend from
background/maintenance spend. Part of the bucket key, so each kind
accumulates into its own row.
fields.name: kind

fields.description:
ProviderName and ProviderModelName are derived fields the
GraphQL resolver populates by joining to the providers table
after the rows load. They are NOT persisted (the providers
table is the source of truth — copying the name into each
usage row would stale on rename). The fields exist so the
usage dashboard can show "Anthropic / claude-3-5-sonnet"
labels for providers that are not in the caller's authorized
list (system summarizer / embedder providers used on the
caller's behalf).
fields.name: providerName

fields.description:
ConversationMessage is a single transcript entry. Content,
ToolCalls, Usage, and Metadata are stored as JSON blobs in
`jsonb` columns — the runner's prompt builder unmarshals on
load, the resolvers pass-through to the GraphQL caller as
opaque Data scalars.

Pairing invariant: every assistant message with non-empty
ToolCalls MUST be followed by tool messages whose ToolCallID
covers each call. Recovery (see docs/subsystems/ai.md "Cancelled /
interrupted tool calls") synthesizes [cancelled] tool rows
when a run dies between persisting the assistant message and
persisting the tool results.
fields.name: message

fields.description: AnswerSdp is the media server's answer, when reconnected.
fields.name: answerSdp

fields.description: MediaSessionID names the new session, when reconnected.
fields.name: mediaSessionId

fields.description: Outcome says whether the client has a new session or should stop.
fields.name: outcome

fields.description:
TicketComment is a reply on a Ticket. Comments form the conversation
shown beneath the ticket detail; the order is by
CreatedAt ascending. Comments are markdown-only on the wire (same
convention as Ticket.Description); the frontend offers both a
plaintext editor and a WYSIWYG editor and serializes both down to
markdown.

Comments support a soft IsInternal flag. Internal comments are
visible only to members of an administrator organization (Mujin
support staff); they are stripped from reads served to regular
org members. Setting IsInternal=true is similarly gated to
admin-org callers — a customer org member cannot mark their own
comment as internal, since "internal" means staff-side.

Edit (a revision) and delete (a soft delete) follow the conversation
mode resolved at startup, reported by SystemInfo.ticketConversationMutable:
mutable unless an immutable support desk is declared. When append-only,
removal is a gated, audited redaction. The original request (the first
comment, flagged IsOriginalRequest) follows the same rule.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: ticketComment

fields.description: PushDevice is the stored registration.
fields.name: pushDevice

fields.description:
Application identifies which Mujin product this release belongs
to. Free-form string — today the only value in production is
"appcontroller", but storing it on the row keeps the schema
open for future products without a migration. Matches the
docker label "PROJECT" on the controller image.
fields.name: application

fields.description:
Attachments is the virtual outputonly list of files referenced
from Changelog via `attachment:<id>` tokens. Populated by the
resolver layer.
fields.name: attachments

fields.description:
Changelog is the release-notes markdown body. Localized: same
(locale, text) list shape as Description, resolved via
LookupLocalizedString. Edited in place on every ModifyRelease
— there is no per-edit revision history. Embedded attachment
tokens (`attachment:<id>`) inside each locale's markdown are
re-linked against the row on every write through the same
attachmentref pipeline page.go uses for revision content.
fields.name: changelog

fields.description:
Channel is the access-control channel name. Derived, never
operator-supplied: every mutation that parses VersionString
stamps Channel with the version's "+..." build suffix, so
"0.45.0+mts" lands on channel "mts" and a suffix-less
"0.45.0" lands on the default channel (""). Visible to users
whose Site.Channels contain the value; admin-org admins always
see every channel.

IMPORTANT: do not leak channel names across tenants. Resolver
list filters and GetRelease both gate on this; mismatched IDs
return not-found rather than forbidden so the existence of a
special-channel release is never confirmable from outside the
channel.
fields.name: channel

fields.description: Timestamp when the release was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
CreatedByUserID is the admin-org administrator who created the
row. Audit only; never used for authz.
fields.name: createdByUserId

fields.description:
DeletedAt is set when DeleteRelease lands. Soft delete — the
row is kept so historical controller→release links remain
resolvable. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows by default.
fields.name: deletedAt

fields.description:
Description is the short one-liner shown alongside the name in
list views. Localized: callers send a list of (locale, text)
entries and the resolver layer renders the entry that matches
the requesting user's locale (English fallback via
LookupLocalizedString). Free-form, optional — an empty slice
means no description in any locale. The long-form release
notes live in Changelog with the same localized shape.
fields.name: description

fields.description:
Images is the virtual outputonly list of ReleaseImage rows tied
to this release. Populated by the resolver layer so the
frontend can render the per-preset / per-hardware image table
without a follow-up query.
fields.name: images

fields.description: Timestamp when the release was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
ModifiedByUserID is the admin-org administrator behind the
latest edit. Audit only.
fields.name: modifiedByUserId

fields.description:
Name is the operator-supplied display label, typically the
canonical version string (e.g. "0.45.0+mts"). Stored
separately from the parsed version columns so admins can
override the rendering without affecting matching.
fields.name: name

fields.description:
Status is the lifecycle state — draft / published / withdrawn.
Manually flipped by an admin-org admin via ModifyRelease.
fields.name: status

fields.description:
VersionMajor / VersionMinor / VersionPatch / VersionPrereleaseLabel /
VersionPrereleaseNumber / VersionBuild are the parsed
components of VersionString, indexed for cheap matching by the
release linker (controller image VERSION label → Release row).
All are output-only — input comes through VersionString /
Name; the resolver runs releaseversion.Parse before writing.

VersionPatch is nullable — "0.45-base" style two-segment
versions have no patch.
VersionPrereleaseNumber is nullable — "0.45-base" has the
label "base" with no number.
VersionBuild is the "+..." suffix; empty when absent.
fields.name: versionMajor

fields.description:
VersionString is the canonical re-encoding of the parsed
version columns below — what the UI renders and what the linker
matches against. Populated from the operator-supplied Name on
every mutation that touches version data, so a typo in Name
produces a parser error before any row is written.
fields.name: versionString

fields.description: Timestamp when the image row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
CreatedByUserID is the admin-org administrator who registered
the image. Audit only.
fields.name: createdByUserId

fields.description:
Digest is the sha256 digest of the manifest as observed at
upload time. The linker prefers digest matching when the
controller's running container has a recorded ImageID — but
most fleets don't, so the labels below are the workhorse
matchers.
fields.name: digest

fields.description: LabelBuild is the "BUILD" docker label — typically "release".
fields.name: labelBuild

fields.description:
LabelBuildDatetime is the "BUILDDATETIME" docker label —
when the image was built. Stored as a typed timestamp so it
can be sorted and rendered locale-aware.
fields.name: labelBuildDatetime

fields.description:
LabelBuildTool is the "BUILDTOOL" docker label — the commit
SHA of the jhbuild/release-tool that produced the image.
fields.name: labelBuildTool

fields.description:
LabelHardwares is the "HARDWARES" docker label split on
whitespace — the hardware models the image supports
(e.g. ["ECS-8000", "ECS-9000", "MCX"]). DB storage is the raw
space-delimited string; the model layer parses on read and
re-joins on write so GraphQL / CLI / LLM-tool callers see a
structured list.
fields.name: labelHardwares

fields.description:
LabelHead is the "HEAD" docker label — the git commit SHA the
image was built at. Primary signal for the exact-vs-version-only
match decision in the linker.
fields.name: labelHead

fields.description:
LabelModuleSet is the "MODULESET" docker label —
e.g. "releaseappcontroller".
fields.name: labelModuleSet

fields.description:
LabelModules is the "MODULES" docker label split on
whitespace — the jhbuild modules baked into the image. Same
split/join contract as LabelHardwares.
fields.name: labelModules

fields.description:
LabelPreset is the "PRESET" docker label — e.g. "mcx",
"ecs9000". A release commonly carries several presets; the
linker matches a controller's running preset against this
column.
fields.name: labelPreset

fields.description:
LabelProducts is the "PRODUCTS" docker label split on
whitespace — the MUJIN_PRODUCT_ID values the image is
licensed for. Same split/join contract as LabelHardwares.
fields.name: labelProducts

fields.description:
LabelProject is the "PROJECT" docker label — e.g.
"appcontroller". The linker uses it together with Release.Application
to scope candidate rows.
fields.name: labelProject

fields.description:
LabelVersion is the "VERSION" docker label as observed on the
image — e.g. "0.45.1.mts" or "0.46.0-rc0.stable.<custom>". The
linker extracts the major.minor.patch core via
releaseversion.ParseImageVersion (channel, prerelease, custom
suffix, and the trailing ".YYYYMMDDTHHMM" timestamp are ignored)
and matches a release on that core.
fields.name: labelVersion

fields.description: Timestamp when the image row was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
ModifiedByUserID is the admin-org administrator behind the
latest edit. Audit only.
fields.name: modifiedByUserId

fields.description:
Registry is the image registry host (e.g.
"docker.mujin.co.jp"). Stored separately from Repository /
Tag so a future deploy-time registry rewrite (e.g. mirror) is
a single column update.
fields.name: registry

fields.description:
ReleaseID is the owning Release. Set at create time, never
modified — moving an image to a different release would
silently re-link every controller that pointed at it.
fields.name: releaseId

fields.description: Repository is the registry path (e.g. "controller/appcontroller").
fields.name: repository

fields.description:
Tag is the registry tag (e.g.
"release.0.45-base.20260518T2045.mcx-7"). Together with
Registry + Repository this is the full reference an operator
would `docker pull`.
fields.name: tag

fields.description: IsStarted is always false: no pass is started on request any more.
fields.name: isStarted

fields.description:
Chat is a room where people talk, and the assistant too when someone
addresses it. What is said is stored once, as ChatMessage rows; each member
has a conversation of kind chat that points here and holds only what is
private to them. OrganizationID is the customer organization of the
members, or the administrator organization when every member is a Mujin
user. There is no administrator reach into a chat: it is read by its
members and nobody else.
fields.name: chat

fields.description: Controller is the row after returning to Launchpad or moving to the selected site.
fields.name: controller

fields.description:
Group is an organization-owned named bundle of sites that replaces
the direct user<->site relationship: users join groups (user_group),
a group carries a set of sites (group_site) and a set of roles
(group_role) that apply at every one of its sites (the uniform group
model). A user's effective site memberships and per-site permission
grants are the union across every group they belong to.

coordination state described in docs/subsystems/ai.md "Stateless across
portal instances": ActiveRun* says which pod is currently running

recreated from the snapshot's VolumeSnapshot data sources, so the VC
keeps its id, subdomain, and credentials. The snapshot row itself is
preserved across a restore so the same point-in-time can be rolled

fields.description:
SSHKey is one customer-owned SSH public key. The row is minted at
"add SSH key" time on the portal frontend; the customer pastes a
public key (`ssh-ed25519 AAAA…` form) and the portal stores only
the public half — there is no portal-side keypair generation, no
private material stored, no preshared key. Authorized_keys-style.

Authentication on the inbound :20022 SSH listener: a bare key
(i.e. not an *ssh.Certificate) presented at handshake time is
looked up by raw bytes against this table; a hit means "user X
is connecting" and the post-auth path enforces org-level access
to the controllers / virtual controllers the user wants to
port-forward to. Cert offers signed by the controller CA take
the existing controller branch and never reach this table.

Postgres is the global source of truth across regions. Unlike
WireGuardPeer there is no in-memory cache and no Redis pub/sub:
SSH connect rate is low enough that a per-connect indexed
SELECT on (public_key) is cheap, and a Create / Revoke is
visible to the next inbound connection without any propagation
step.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: sshKey

fields.description:
WireGuardPeer is one customer-owned WireGuard device. The row is
minted at "add device" time on the portal frontend; the customer
installs the returned wg-quick config on the device and then dials
the regional WG endpoint over UDP to reach controllers and virtual
controllers their organization owns.

The peer's in-tunnel address is derived from the public key, not
stored — `fd00:1:` + the leading 96 bits of `blake2b(public_key)`.
Every pod recomputes the address on demand, so there is no
allocator and no IP column to migrate. Same for controller and
virtual-controller synthetic addresses (`fd00:c::/32`,
`fd00:d::/32`); see WIREGUARD_PLAN.md.

Postgres is the global source of truth across regions; per-region
Redis carries `wireguard:peers:event` notifications for in-region
pods to apply changes inline. Cross-region propagation rides on the
30 s reconcile loop in backend/wg.

The private key is **never** persisted server-side. It is generated
on the request goroutine that mints the device, embedded in the
returned wg-quick config, and dropped from memory once the response
is flushed. The pubkey + preshared key in this row are sufficient
for the portal to authenticate handshakes and decrypt session
keys; reissuing a device is a revoke + remint cycle.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
