fields.description:
RejectSession revokes a pending magic-link session with its
secret (the "this wasn't me" link).
fields.name: RejectSession

args.description:
Kind is one of recurrence_of / duplicate_of / related. Ignored on
unrelate.
args.name: kind

fields.description: RelateIncidents links two incidents or retypes an existing link.
fields.name: RelateIncidents

fields.description:
RememberConversation is retired and does nothing: conversations and chats
are filed automatically. It returns isStarted false so releases that still
call it keep working.
fields.name: RememberConversation

args.description: UserID is who to remove; empty means the caller leaves.
args.name: userId

fields.description:
RemoveChatMember takes someone out of a chat; with no userId it is the
caller leaving.
fields.name: RemoveChatMember

args.description: ID of the Controller to unlink.
args.name: controllerId

args.description: SiteID optionally names a destination; omitted returns the controller to Launchpad.
args.name: siteId

fields.description:
RemoveControllerLink releases a Controller to Mujin/Launchpad by default,
or moves it to an explicitly selected site. The default return requires
controller:link over the owning organization; an explicit destination
uses the ordinary site assignment and cross-organization transfer gates.
fields.name: RemoveControllerLink

fields.description:
RemoveMessageLinkPreviews removes the previews of a message the caller
said.
fields.name: RemoveMessageLinkPreviews

fields.description:
RemoveReleaseImages is the batch form of RemoveReleaseImage — many
release images removed atomically, gated per image; the whole
batch rolls back if any image is rejected.
fields.name: RemoveReleaseImages

fields.description:
RemoveSiteFromGroup removes a site from the group's site set.
Idempotent.
fields.name: RemoveSiteFromGroup

fields.description:
RemoveUserFromGroup removes a (user, group) membership.
Idempotent.
fields.name: RemoveUserFromGroup

fields.description:
RemoveUsersFromGroup removes many users from one group in a
single atomic call. Idempotent per pair.
fields.name: RemoveUsersFromGroup

fields.description:
RenameConversation gives a conversation a title a person chose; the
summarizer leaves it alone from then on.
fields.name: RenameConversation

fields.description:
ReopenGoal brings a met or stopped goal back to work. Its owner and the
administrators of its organization may.
fields.name: ReopenGoal

args.description:
ReporterID names the tab or the app install, so one going out of sight
hides only itself.
args.name: reporterId

args.description: Source is web or app; empty means web.
args.name: source

fields.description:
ReportAgentPresence says the caller has Portal or the app in front of them
and how long since their last input. Visible web tabs and the app send it
every minute. The report is kept in Redis for two minutes and never stored
in the database. The answer names a conversation the assistant started on
its own a moment ago, so the chat box can open on it.
fields.name: ReportAgentPresence

args.description:
ShouldAllowRiskWithoutAsking is "always allow this kind": with an
approval it also stores the conversation owner's choice to let calls of
the approval's risk run without asking. Only the owner can pass it.
args.name: shouldAllowRiskWithoutAsking

args.description:
OrganizationID is the tenant to read/act on. Empty defaults to the
caller's own organization.
args.name: organizationId

args.description: OAuthConsentID identifies the consent grant to revoke.
args.name: oauthConsentId

fields.description:
RevokeOAuthConsent withdraws one of the caller's consent grants
and revokes every refresh token descending from it. The client's
outstanding access tokens are short-lived JWTs that expire on
their own; with the consent gone the next /authorize shows the
consent screen again.
fields.name: RevokeOAuthConsent

fields.description:
RevokeOAuthConsents is the batch form of RevokeOAuthConsent —
many grants revoked atomically, gated per grant; the whole batch
rolls back on any error.
fields.name: RevokeOAuthConsents

fields.description:
RevokeSSHKey marks the key revoked. The next inbound
SSH-handshake DB lookup excludes the row, so authentication
fails immediately — no propagation step needed.
fields.name: RevokeSSHKey

fields.description:
RevokeSSHKeys is the batch form of RevokeSSHKey — many keys revoked
atomically, gated per key; the whole batch rolls back on any error.
fields.name: RevokeSSHKeys

args.description: ID of the Session to revoke.
args.name: sessionId

fields.description:
RevokeSession revokes one of the caller's other sessions. Revoking
the current session is rejected; use Logout for that.
fields.name: RevokeSession

args.description: ID of the Token to revoke.
args.name: tokenId

fields.description:
Revoke an API token. The row stays in the database with RevokedAt
stamped — the auth path treats revoked tokens as missing, but the
settings UI can still show "Revoked <ago>".
fields.name: RevokeToken

fields.description:
RevokeTokens is the batch form of RevokeToken — many tokens revoked
atomically, gated per token; the whole batch rolls back on any
error (e.g. trying to revoke the caller's own session token).
fields.name: RevokeTokens

fields.description:
RevokeWireGuardPeer marks a peer revoked and publishes a
revoke event. The pod-level peer cache removes the peer from
the wireguard-go device within milliseconds in-region, or at
the next reconcile (≤30s) cross-region.
fields.name: RevokeWireGuardPeer

fields.description: RingChatCallMembers rings members of the chat who are not on the call.
fields.name: RingChatCallMembers

args.description: OAuthClientID identifies the confidential client to re-key.
args.name: oauthClientId

fields.description:
RotateOAuthClientSecret mints a new client secret for a
confidential client and returns it once. Administrator-only.
fields.name: RotateOAuthClientSecret

args.description:
CellSetupPatch preserves omitted sections. A present selection with no IDs
clears membership; a present empty Production clears all preferences.
Measurement selections remain unqualified drafts until source contracts are verified.
args.name: setup

fields.description:
SaveSiteMaterialFlow replaces a site's topology, not Cell measurement
settings. Initial creation expects revision zero. Stale drafts conflict.
fields.name: SaveSiteMaterialFlow

args.description:
InterruptedAnswer is the spoken answer the sender talked over to say
this message, so the assistant knows what they did not hear. Only a
voice message carries it; it is cut to a bounded length, never stored.
args.name: interruptedAnswer

args.description:
Mentions are the names the sender chose from the mention list, with their
place in the message. Chats only; a message in a conversation with the
assistant ignores them.
args.name: mentions

args.description:
ReplyToMessageID names the earlier message this one answers. In a chat, a
reply to a message the assistant said addresses the assistant. In a
conversation with the assistant the server reads the message itself and
stores a bounded quote (replyToExcerpt, replyToAuthorName) with the new
one, which the model is shown as a reference; the client sends only the
id.
args.name: replyToMessageId

args.description:
Surface is where the answer is read, so the reply is written for it:
a table on a wide screen, none on a phone, plain text in a terminal.
args.name: surface

args.description:
Viewing is the page the sender has open. The server checks the
sender may see it and silently drops it when they may not, so a send
never fails on it and never confirms that a resource exists.
args.name: viewing

args.description:
Voice marks a message sent from an active voice call so the run
steers the reply toward brief, spoken-friendly output.
args.name: voice

args.description:
VoiceMessage makes the message a voice message of a chat: the sender's
own audio upload, its length and its waveform. Message must then be
empty. A voice message starts no turn of the assistant.
args.name: voiceMessage

args.description:
IsSpeakFirstEnabled lets the assistant start conversations with the
organization's people. Left out, it stays as it is.
args.name: isSpeakFirstEnabled

fields.description:
SetAgentBackgroundSetting turns goals, found ideas and the assistant
starting conversations on or off for an organization. Organization administrators.
fields.name: SetAgentBackgroundSetting

args.description:
CostLimitCurrency is a three-letter code; empty uses the platform default
currency.
args.name: costLimitCurrency

fields.description:
SetAgentCostLimit replaces an organization's cost limits. A limit left out
is not set, so the platform default applies; 0 is no limit for this
organization. Amounts are nano units of costLimitCurrency. Organization
administrators.
fields.name: SetAgentCostLimit

args.description:
DreamProviderID picks the provider for a dream's calls; an empty string
uses the main agent's.
args.name: dreamProviderId

args.description:
A field left out keeps the value the organization has now (the defaults
when it has none), so a call can change one switch.
args.name: isDreamEnabled

fields.description:
SetAgentDreamSetting turns dreaming on or off for an organization and sets
its budget. Organization administrators. The administrator who turns it on
is the user the dream's spend is recorded on.
fields.name: SetAgentDreamSetting

fields.description:
SetAgentMemoryFiling turns remembering the caller's own conversations on
or off.
fields.name: SetAgentMemoryFiling

fields.description:
SetAgentSpeakFirst turns the assistant starting conversations on or off
for the caller.
fields.name: SetAgentSpeakFirst

fields.description:
SetAgentSpeakFirstReason turns one reason the assistant starts a
conversation on or off for the caller.
fields.name: SetAgentSpeakFirstReason

fields.description:
SetAgentSpeechVoice chooses the voice the assistant speaks with in the
caller's calls. An empty voice goes back to the default.
fields.name: SetAgentSpeechVoice

fields.description:
SetAgentToolPreference lets agent tool calls of one risk run without
asking (true) or asks first again (false). It applies to the caller's
interactive runs, and decides which calls an unattended run of the
caller (a scheduled job or a sub-agent) may make at all.
fields.name: SetAgentToolPreference

args.description: Enabled turns auto-reload on or off.
args.name: enabled

args.description:
Threshold is the balance level at/below which a reload
fires; Amount is how much each reload charges. Both in the
org's billing-currency minor units.
args.name: threshold

fields.description:
SetChatCallMedia tells the others the caller is muted or unmuted and has
the camera on or off. The tracks themselves change with replaceTrack on
the client, so no new negotiation is needed.
fields.name: SetChatCallMedia

fields.description:
SetChatCallTranscription turns recording and transcription of the call on
or off. Nobody is asked: everyone on the call, and anyone who joins later,
is told who turned it on. The person who turned it on pays.
fields.name: SetChatCallTranscription

args.description: Subscriptions are at most 64 entries.
args.name: subscriptions

fields.description:
SetChatCallVideoSubscriptions chooses which video the caller receives:
for each person named, the full layer, the small layer or nothing. The
server applies it without renegotiation, switching layers on a key frame.
People not named keep their earlier choice, and the default for everyone
is small. The caller must be on the call (after JoinChatCallMedia) and
every person named must be too; the caller's own entry is ignored. Send
it again after reconnecting the media.
fields.name: SetChatCallVideoSubscriptions

fields.description: SetChatMemoryFiling lets a chat be filed into its organization's memory.
fields.name: SetChatMemoryFiling

fields.description: SetChatTyping tells the other members the caller is writing.
fields.name: SetChatTyping

args.description:
BackupIntervalSeconds is the cadence to honor when
IsBackupEnabled is true. Must be one of
ControllerBackupIntervalSecondsAllowed; ignored (stored as 0)
when IsBackupEnabled is false. The closed set keeps the column
from drifting into a cadence the controller-side scheduler has
not been vetted against.
args.name: backupIntervalSeconds

args.description: ID of the Controller whose backup settings to update.
args.name: controllerId

args.description:
IsBackupEnabled toggles the portal-driven backup path advertised
on /api/v1/controller/info. False suppresses uploads
regardless of BackupIntervalSeconds.
args.name: isBackupEnabled

fields.description:
SetControllerBackupSettings flips the per-controller portal-driven
backup policy advertised on /api/v1/controller/info. The pair is
validated server-side: enabled=true requires an IntervalSeconds in
ControllerBackupIntervalSecondsAllowed; enabled=false stores
IntervalSeconds=0 regardless of input so the persisted shape is
unambiguous.
fields.name: SetControllerBackupSettings

args.description: ID of the Controller whose webstack credentials to set.
args.name: controllerId

args.description:
Password is the plaintext controller webstack password. It is
sealed in-memory and never persisted in the clear. Empty resets
it to the mujin default. Username and Password are always set as
a pair — the password is write-only, so it cannot be preserved
across a username-only edit.
args.name: password

args.description:
Username for HTTP basic auth. Empty resets it to the mujin
default. Stored in the clear (it is not a secret).
args.name: username

fields.description:
SetControllerCredentials sets the controller webstack username and
password together; the password is sealed at rest. The pair rides
its own mutation rather than ControllerInput because the password
is write-only (mirrors SetProviderAPIKey).
fields.name: SetControllerCredentials

args.description: ID of the Controller whose sync filter to save.
args.name: controllerId

args.description:
Filter is the webstack filter for the resource type. Only log and stat
entries take one, a single operation on their type name. Null clears
the saved filter, so the type's current default applies.
args.name: filter

args.description:
ResourceType whose filter to save. Account is rejected, its filter is
locked to constant-true.
args.name: resourceType

fields.description:
SetControllerSyncResourceFilter saves the sync filter one resource type
is applied with when sync is next enabled, or clears it when the filter
is null so the type's current default applies. Platform administrators
only, while sync is off. Account is rejected: its filter is locked to
constant-true.
fields.name: SetControllerSyncResourceFilter

args.description: ID of the Controller whose sync settings to update.
args.name: controllerId

args.description:
IsSyncEnabled toggles the portal-driven data-sync path advertised
on /api/v1/controller/info.
args.name: isSyncEnabled

args.description:
SyncIntervalSeconds is the push cadence the portal dictates, in seconds,
advertised on Sync.intervalSeconds. Omitted (null) leaves the stored
cadence unchanged (partial update); an explicit zero means the portal
does not dictate one and the controller falls back to its webstack.conf
push interval. Reset to zero when isSyncEnabled is false.
args.name: syncIntervalSeconds

args.description:
SyncResourceTypes is the explicit set of resource types to sync, each
full-synced. Empty or omitted syncs nothing.
args.name: syncResourceTypes

fields.description:
SetControllerSyncSettings flips the per-controller portal-driven
data-sync policy advertised on /api/v1/controller/info and stores the
resource selection plus the push cadence (SyncIntervalSeconds is a
partial update: nil leaves the stored cadence unchanged, zero clears
it). enabled=false clears the selection and the cadence regardless of
input so the persisted shape is unambiguous.
fields.name: SetControllerSyncSettings

fields.description:
SetDefaultGroup moves the organization's default-group marker —
the group a newly provisioned member joins when they would
otherwise land in zero groups — to the given group. The previous
default is demoted in the same mutation. Same administrator gate
as the other group mutations.
fields.name: SetDefaultGroup

args.description: Kind discriminates which resource the TargetID points at.
args.name: kind

args.description:
TargetID is the id of the favorited resource (Site, Controller,
or VirtualController, depending on Kind).
args.name: targetId

fields.description:
SetGlobalKnowledgeSetting switches the filing of general product knowledge
from staff conversations and the dream of the global pool on or off. A field
left out keeps its value. The administrator who turns the dream on is the
user its spend is recorded on. Platform administrators.
fields.name: SetGlobalKnowledgeSetting

fields.description:
SetGroupRoles replaces the group's entire role set in a single
atomic call: roles in the desired set but not yet bound are added,
roles currently bound but absent are removed. A bound role applies
at every site the group carries (the uniform group model).
fields.name: SetGroupRoles

args.description: ActivityStatus is "active" or "cleared".
args.name: activityStatus

fields.description:
SetIncidentActivityStatus overrides whether the condition is still
present on the floor, and stops the detector owning that field.
fields.name: SetIncidentActivityStatus

args.description:
CellID is the cell within the incident's own site. Empty clears
the scoping back to the whole site.
args.name: cellId

fields.description:
SetIncidentCell re-scopes an incident to a cell within its own
site, or clears it with an empty cellId.
fields.name: SetIncidentCell

fields.description:
SetMainConversation makes one of the caller's own conversations with the
main assistant their main chat. The main chat before it becomes a side chat.
fields.name: SetMainConversation

args.description:
MinimumAlarmLevel is the per-channel severity floor; only meaningful
for the alarm kind on an outbound channel. Empty leaves it unset.
args.name: minimumAlarmLevel

args.description: IsActive is the new value of the soft activation flag.
args.name: isActive

args.description: ID of the Organization whose IsActive flag is being changed.
args.name: organizationId

fields.description:
SetOrganizationActive toggles Organization.IsActive.
Cross-organization administrator only; the caller cannot
deactivate their own organization.
fields.name: SetOrganizationActive

args.description:
MemoryFilingProviderID picks the provider for the filing call; empty uses
each agent's main provider.
args.name: memoryFilingProviderId

fields.description:
SetOrganizationAgentSetting turns remembering conversations on or off for
an organization, and picks the provider for the call. Organization
administrators.
fields.name: SetOrganizationAgentSetting

args.description: IsActive is the new value of the soft activation flag.
args.name: isActive

args.description: IDs of the Organizations whose IsActive flag is being changed.
args.name: organizationIds

fields.description:
SetOrganizationsActive is the batch form of SetOrganizationActive
— one is-active value applied to many organizations atomically,
gated per organization; the whole batch rolls back if any
organization is rejected.
fields.name: SetOrganizationsActive

fields.description: SetPlanModelPrice creates or replaces one per-model price of a plan.
fields.name: SetPlanModelPrice

args.description:
APIKey is the plaintext upstream key. Empty clears the key.
Sealed in-memory and never persisted in the clear.
args.name: apiKey

fields.description:
SetSiteArchived flips Site.IsArchived. Per-user org admin in
the site's organization (same gate as ModifySite). Reversible.
fields.name: SetSiteArchived

fields.description:
SetSiteChannels replaces the site's release-access channel
set. Admin-org admin only — a customer-org admin must never
be able to opt their site into another tenant's channel and
gain visibility into the catalog rows on it.
fields.name: SetSiteChannels

fields.description:
SetSitesArchived is the batch form of SetSiteArchived — one
is-archived value applied to many sites atomically, gated per
site; the whole batch rolls back if any site is rejected.
fields.name: SetSitesArchived

args.description:
ClearWarning removes any custom warning threshold (since a nil
Warning otherwise means "leave unchanged").
args.name: clearWarning

args.description:
SpendingLimit is the org-wide overage spend ceiling for the
cycle, in the org's billing-currency minor units. nil clears the
limit (no cap; balance is then the only ceiling).
args.name: spendingLimit

args.description:
Warning is the soft warning ceiling (below the spending
limit) that fires a notification when crossed, in minor units. When
ClearWarning is false and this is nil the warning is left unchanged.
args.name: warning

fields.description:
Participant-model mutations. SetTicketAssignee sets the single
accountable owner (empty clears); SetTicketRequester reassigns the
requester (support-only, ticket:assign). AddTicketCollaborator /
RemoveTicketCollaborator manage the internal staff list;
AddTicketCc / RemoveTicketCc manage the external CC list (the
manager enforces the CC-authorization policy).
fields.name: SetTicketAssignee

fields.description:
SetTicketExternalStatus records the provider's raw status provenance on
a mirrored ticket. Platform-administrator only — the ticketsync daemon's
seam, like the on-behalf authorUserId on CreateTicket.
fields.name: SetTicketExternalStatus

args.description: IsActive is the new value of the soft activation flag.
args.name: isActive

args.description: ID of the User whose IsActive flag is being changed.
args.name: userId

fields.description:
SetUserActive toggles User.IsActive. Gated to organization
administrators over the target user's organization; the
caller cannot deactivate themselves.
fields.name: SetUserActive

args.description:
SpendingLimit is the per-user overage cap in the org's
billing-currency minor units, applied to every member. nil clears the
cap (no per-user limit).
args.name: spendingLimit

fields.description:
SetUserSpendingLimit sets the org-wide per-user spending cap — a single
value applied uniformly to every member.
fields.name: SetUserSpendingLimit

fields.description:
SetVirtualControllersPaused / DestroyVirtualControllers are the
batch forms of the single-VC pause-toggle / destroy mutations,
applied across many VCs atomically and gated per VC.
fields.name: SetVirtualControllersPaused

args.description: IsSnoozed true snoozes for a day; false ends a snooze.
args.name: isSnoozed

fields.description:
SnoozeAgentSpeakFirst keeps the assistant from starting conversations
with the caller for a day, or ends the snooze.
fields.name: SnoozeAgentSpeakFirst

args.description: IsVideoOn starts the caller's camera on.
args.name: isVideoOn

args.description:
UserIDs are the members to ring; all other members are not rung. Left
out, every member is rung.
args.name: userIds

fields.description:
StartChatCall starts a call in a chat the caller is in and rings the
chosen members, or every member when userIds is left out. Starting in a
chat that already has a going call returns that call and rings no one.
fields.name: StartChatCall

fields.description:
StartDirectChat opens the direct chat with one person, or returns the one
the pair already has.
fields.name: StartDirectChat

fields.description:
StartGlobalMemoryDream dreams the global pool now, in the background,
whether or not it is due. Platform administrators.
fields.name: StartGlobalMemoryDream

args.description:
CheckIntervalMinutes is the wait between the goal's turns at first; zero
means an hour.
args.name: checkIntervalMinutes

fields.description:
StartGoal starts a goal for the caller. The organization has to have
turned goals on, and the caller may have only a few in progress.
fields.name: StartGoal

fields.description:
StartGoalFromIdea starts an idea as a goal the assistant works on in the
background, instead of drafting it as a request.
fields.name: StartGoalFromIdea

args.description:
IdeaID is the idea's id; a catalog idea that was not answered yet has the
id "catalog:" followed by its key.
args.name: ideaId

fields.description:
StartIdea marks an idea started and returns its request as a draft. It
runs nothing and sends nothing.
fields.name: StartIdea

args.description: UserID of the user to impersonate.
args.name: userId

fields.description:
StartImpersonation mints a short-lived impersonation token for
the target user and swaps the portal session onto it. Gated to
organization administrators over the target's organization
(cross-org administrators reach every org).
fields.name: StartImpersonation

fields.description:
StartMemoryDream dreams an organization now, in the background, whether or
not it is due. Organization administrators.
fields.name: StartMemoryDream

fields.description:
StopGoal ends a goal before it was met. Its owner and the administrators
of its organization may.
fields.name: StopGoal

args.description:
AttachmentIDs are the caller's own uploads, such as the screenshot
that opened the feedback drawer.
args.name: attachmentIds

args.description: ClientSurface says what sent it: ios, android, web or cli.
args.name: clientSurface

args.description:
ClientVersion, DeviceName, SystemVersion and ScreenName describe the
client for whoever reproduces the fault. All optional.
args.name: clientVersion

args.description: FeedbackText is what the person wrote about Portal itself.
args.name: feedbackText

fields.description:
SubscribeTicket / UnsubscribeTicket toggle the *caller's* own
subscription (self-service — there is no target user argument).
Gated only on the caller being able to see the ticket, so any
participant can follow / unfollow it. To subscribe someone else,
@-mention them. Returns the refreshed subscriber list.
fields.name: SubscribeTicket

args.description: IsEnabled toggles the subscription without removing it.
args.name: isEnabled

args.description:
MinimumConfidence is a detector-confidence floor in 0..1. A site
producing many low-confidence detections can be watched for only
the ones worth interrupting someone over.
args.name: minimumConfidence

fields.description:
SubscribeToSiteIncidents starts (or updates) the caller's
subscription to a site's incidents.
fields.name: SubscribeToSiteIncidents

fields.description:
TellGoal gives a goal the caller's words. A goal that waited for them
goes back to work in a minute.
fields.name: TellGoal

fields.description:
TransferSite reassigns a site to a destination organization.
Admin-org admin only — never a customer-org operation.
Updates site.organization_id and every controller currently in
the site to the destination org (preserving the controller↔site
same-org invariant). Tickets that reference the moved site keep
their owning org and lose the site association so the
destination org can't see them. group_site entries carrying the
site are dropped — destination org admins re-grant through their
own groups.
fields.name: TransferSite

args.description:
DuplicateOfIncidentID records what this one duplicates, when that
is the reason for dismissing or resolving it. Links the two
through the ordinary duplicate_of relation.
args.name: duplicateOfIncidentId

fields.description:
TransitionIncident moves an incident through its review
lifecycle and stamps the reviewer.
fields.name: TransitionIncident

fields.description: UnlinkIncidentTicket removes an incident-to-ticket link.
fields.name: UnlinkIncidentTicket

args.description: DeviceToken is the device token to remove.
args.name: deviceToken

args.description: Platform is ios or android. Left out means ios.
args.name: platform

fields.description:
UnregisterPushDevice removes the caller's registration of a device token,
for signing out or turning notifications off in the app.
fields.name: UnregisterPushDevice

args.description:
Kind is one of recurrence_of / duplicate_of / related. Ignored on
unrelate.
args.name: kind

fields.description: UnrelateIncidents removes a link between two incidents.
fields.name: UnrelateIncidents

args.description: Kind discriminates which resource the TargetID points at.
args.name: kind

args.description:
TargetID is the id of the favorited resource (Site, Controller,
or VirtualController, depending on Kind).
args.name: targetId

fields.description: UnsubscribeFromSiteIncidents removes the caller's subscription.
fields.name: UnsubscribeFromSiteIncidents

args.description:
Optional code to authorize the Session; it can also be authorized
via AuthorizeSession.
args.name: code

args.description: Ticket for exchanging a Session
args.name: ticket

fields.description:
ValidateSession exchanges a ticket plus OTP code for a session
bearer token, enforcing the per-ticket failed-attempt lockout.
fields.name: ValidateSession

args.description:
ShouldCollapseThreads counts the main history, as ListConversationMessages
reads it with the same argument.
args.name: shouldCollapseThreads

fields.description:
CountConversationMessages says how many messages a conversation holds,
so a client that loaded the latest page can offer the earlier ones.
fields.name: CountConversationMessages

fields.description:
CountUnreadNotifications returns the bell badge count. Trimmed
to the caller; admin-org cross-user reads are not supported
(notifications are owner-scoped).
fields.name: CountUnreadNotifications

args.description: IsWordsOnly searches by words even when an embedding provider exists.
args.name: isWordsOnly

fields.description:
EvaluateMemory puts each question through the search a turn runs over the
caller's own memory and scores what comes back against the facts the
question expects and forbids. It calls no model and writes nothing; with
an embedding provider configured it also searches by meaning, which costs
one embedding call per question. Organization administrators.
fields.name: EvaluateMemory

fields.description:
GetAgentActivityTranscript is the read-only account of what one run did:
its conversation messages and the sections that have no message, such as
the phases of a dream or the request and result of an MCP call. Whoever
may read the run may read its transcript.
fields.name: GetAgentActivityTranscript

fields.description:
GetAgentAvailability reports whether the caller can actually use
the agent surface. Three independent things have to hold, only
one of which the browser could work out for itself, so they are
answered together here rather than inferred from a handful of
queries and their error shapes:

  - the AI feature is configured on this deployment at all
    (no secret box, no agents — a deploy-time fact the client
    otherwise learns only as an error);
  - an enabled main agent exists and the caller's organization
    reaches it (platform administrators always do);
  - at least one enabled provider is authorized for that
    organization, without which a conversation cannot run.

Never errors on a merely unavailable surface: "you cannot use
this" is the answer, not a failure, so a caller can gate a menu
item on it without treating a normal state as a broken query.

LIMIT); After is the number of rows to skip (the SQL OFFSET). Both
are optional — a nil First means "the server's default page size",
a nil/zero After means "the first page".

This replaces the old per-query cursor argument: offset pagination
pairs with a total count to give the UI an exact page count, which
cursor pagination cannot.

args.description:
WatchPaths are dot-paths into each orchestrator's published state,
declaring what the consumer cares about — for example
"productionCycleStatus" or
"warehouseExecutionState.warehouseExecutionStatus". A frame is
emitted only when one of them moves.

Portal never interprets a path, so a new orchestrator type or
controller field works without a portal change. Empty defaults to
the orchestrator base class fields (runStatus, hasError,
statusMessage), which are low-churn. Declaring a path that changes
every frame — a pallet counter, say — will emit every tick.

fields.description:
OnControllerOrchestratorChanged streams orchestrator state changes
for one controller. The first frame carries every orchestrator with
isSnapshot set, so a consumer needs no separate query to establish
current state and cannot lose a transition to the gap between two
calls; later frames carry only the orchestrators whose watched
paths moved.

Access is re-checked on every tick, so losing visibility of the
controller closes the stream rather than leaking further frames.

fields.description:
OnNotification emits an event whenever a notification is written for the
caller, from any pod in any region. Events carry the notification's id
and kind only; the client reads the row with the notification queries, so
the stream can never leak content. Delivery is best-effort: a client
that was disconnected reads the inbox when it reconnects. The socket
authenticates like every subscription, with the bearer token at upgrade,
and closes with 4401 when the token expires or is revoked.
fields.name: OnNotification

fields.description:
OnTicketChanged emits a lightweight event whenever a ticket or
its comment thread changes, portal-wide, filtered to tickets
the caller is allowed to see. Events carry ids only; the
consumer re-reads through the query surface, so the stream can
never leak content. Events are published after the mutation's
transaction commits, so every event refers to a committed
change and a rolled-back mutation emits nothing. Delivery is
still best-effort: a Redis blip can drop an event, so consumers
reconcile rather than apply.

the direct user<->site relationship: users join groups (user_group),

their own organization.

(group_role) that apply at every one of its sites (the uniform group
model). A user's effective site memberships and per-site permission
grants are the union across every group they belong to.

The user owns the conversation; the agent provides the system

recently used Provider so the UI can resume with the same picker
state, but every turn can override via the providerId argument
on sendMessage.

Run-lock and summarizer-claim columns hold the cross-pod
coordination state described in docs/subsystems/ai.md "Stateless across
portal instances": ActiveRun* says which pod is currently running
the conversation and which regional Redis carries its pub/sub
channels; Summarizer* says which pod is generating title/summary.
Both follow the conditional-UPDATE-as-lease pattern.

configuration. The same ProviderType may appear multiple times with
different keys, base URLs, or model names — Name is the
human-readable disambiguator. APIKeyCiphertext stores the AES-GCM
sealed key derived via HKDF from the portal's master secret-file;
see util/secretbox. The plaintext key is never returned over the
wire — UIs render APIKeyFingerprint instead.

without a grant a non-admin caller does not see this provider in

binds to a group via group_role; the role's verbs then fire for every
member of that group across the group's sites. A role may carry both
site-scoped verbs (controller/ticket/page/… actions) and org- or
platform-scoped verbs (user/role/organization management,
platform:administer). Org- and platform-scoped operations resolve
through those verbs on the caller's snapshot — see
backend/access/permission.go for the resolution order.

Owner / Operator / Viewer are seeded per organization at create
time so a fresh tenant has working defaults; nothing distinguishes
them from custom roles at the schema level — DeleteRole refuses to
remove a role that still has active (user, site) bindings, which
is the same safety check that protects any in-use custom role.

non-admin org member can see. Sites belong to a single organization;
a controller is in at most one site (which must be in the
controller's own org); a user can join many sites within their
organization. There is no role distinction inside a site for now —
membership is the whole permission.

Visibility is enforced in backend/access:
  - admin-org members see everything
  - per-user org admins see every controller in their own org
  - regular org members see a controller only when both the
    controller has a site AND they are a member of that site

Site mutations and controller<->site assignments require the per-user
org admin flag, mirroring the link/unlink semantics in apigraph/link.go
(admin-org membership is intentionally not special-cased there).

comment outwards; inbound rows record the external note a portal
comment was created from. Either way the row is the sync daemon's
echo guard — content whose id appears here is a mirror, not new
input — and SyncedBodyHash is the per-comment merge base for edit
propagation.

fields.description:

system (at most one per system) and carries the sync daemon's
merge base: the content hash and state both sides last agreed on.
A side that still matches the merge base did not move, so the
other side's change can be applied to it; when both moved the
portal wins. The row replaces the marker comments the GitLab
daemon originally embedded in issue bodies — those sat in
human-editable space and Zendesk would strip them entirely.

Rows are written only by the sync daemons (admin-org tokens);
see backend/ticketsync and docs/subsystems/ticketsync.md.

fields.description:
Channels is the set of release-access channels the site's
users can see in the release catalog. A release's channel is
the "+..." build suffix of its version ("" for suffix-less
versions), so a site carrying ["", "mts"] — the default for
new sites, see DefaultSiteChannels — sees both the default
catalog and the mts builds. Site membership is the whole
grant: a channel absent from this set is invisible to the
site's members.

Output-only on the GraphQL surface — ModifySite never patches
it. SetSiteChannels is the dedicated mutation, gated by
platform administrators (platform:administer
only): a customer-org admin must not be able to opt their
site into another tenant's channel.

Chat is a room where people talk, and the assistant too when someone
addresses it. What is said is stored once, as ChatMessage rows; each member
has a conversation of kind chat that points here and holds only what is
private to them. OrganizationID is the customer organization of the
members, or the administrator organization when every member is a Mujin
user. There is no administrator reach into a chat: it is read by its

Visibility follows conversations: the owner reads it, an administrator of the
organization reads their organization's, and staff who oversee the assistant
read every organization's.

fields.name: count

fields.description:
M2 is the sum of squared deviations from the mean. Variance does
not merge under the fold; M2 does, and variance is derived at
emit.

Webstack's DistributionMetric.variance is documented as the
SAMPLE variance, so the conversion is M2 = variance * (Weight-1),
not variance * Weight. The two differ by n/(n-1) per group —
invisible at n=1000 and wrong at n=2.
fields.name: m2

fields.description: Max is the largest observation, on a distribution metric.
fields.name: max

fields.description: Min is the smallest observation, on a distribution metric.
fields.name: min

fields.description: Sum is the measure on a distribution metric.
fields.name: sum

fields.description:
Weight is the observation count on a distribution metric, and
the fold's weight. Webstack calls it totalCount.

Weight is NOT a valid denominator for every metric. On
productionCycle.stateDurations it is the aggregator's sample-row
count rather than a cycle count, so Sum/Weight is meaningless
there; MetricMeta.WeightIsObservationCount declares whether a
mean may be derived at all.
fields.name: weight

fields.description:
BackgroundWork is a sub-agent the assistant started and did not wait for. It
runs in a child conversation, survives a restart, and when it finishes it
wakes the conversation that started it with its result.

Visibility follows the conversation that started it: the owner reads it, an
administrator of the organization reads their organization's, and a platform
administrator reads all.
fields.name: backgroundWork

types.description: The `String` scalar type represents textual data, represented as UTF-8 character sequences. The String type is most often used by GraphQL to represent free-form human-readable text.
types.name: String

fields.description:
Ticket is a customer support request belonging to a single
organization. The portal is the source of truth — there is no sync
to an external ticketing system in this version (Zendesk/GitLab
mirrors, if added later, will live in a separate package and write
to a side table rather than reshape this model).

Ticket follows the VirtualController pattern: pointer fields so
partial-update semantics fall out of nil-vs-non-nil; the row is the
source of truth; soft state (assignees, controllers) lives in
many-to-many join tables; comments and attachments are separate
models linked back by ticket_id.

Generated Update() and GetXxx() methods live in models_gen.go.
fields.name: ticket

fields.description:
CurrentPeriodStartedAt / CurrentPeriodEndedAt bound the active billing
cycle. The cost roll-up sums metered usage within this window.
Mirrored from Stripe; output-only.
fields.name: currentPeriodStartedAt

fields.description:
IsCancelAtPeriodEnd is true when the org has scheduled a downgrade to
free: the paid subscription stays billing-active (so the org keeps
what it paid for) until CurrentPeriodEndedAt, when Stripe ends it and
the customer.subscription.deleted webhook drops the org to free. No
mid-cycle refund — the customer simply uses out the cycle. Mirrored
from Stripe's cancel_at_period_end.
fields.name: isCancelAtPeriodEnd

fields.description:
IsEnforcementEnabled is the per-org kill switch for the hard-block
gates. Defaults false so a subscription can be set up and
observed before any action is ever blocked; flipped true once the
org is ready to be held to its budget and caps.
fields.name: isEnforcementEnabled

fields.description:
OrganizationID is the tenant this subscription bills. Unique —
one subscription per organization.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
Plan is the virtual output-only join to the enrolled plan,
populated by the resolver layer so the billing page renders tier
detail without a follow-up query. Not persisted.
fields.name: plan

fields.description: PlanID is the tier this organization is enrolled in.
fields.name: planId

fields.description:
Status mirrors the Stripe subscription state. Written by the
webhook handler; output-only over GraphQL.
fields.name: status

fields.description: Stripe object references. Empty until the org completes Checkout.
fields.name: stripeCustomerId

fields.description:
AppliedFilter is the filter the controller is served for ResourceType,
null while sync is off or the type is not selected.
fields.name: appliedFilter

fields.description:
DefaultFilter is the filter ResourceType is applied with when nothing is
saved.
fields.name: defaultFilter

fields.description:
IsSavedFilterApplied is whether AppliedFilter selects what SavedFilter,
or DefaultFilter when nothing is saved, selects.
fields.name: isSavedFilterApplied

fields.description: ResourceType is the sync resource type.
fields.name: resourceType

fields.description:
SavedFilter is the filter ResourceType is applied with when sync is
next enabled or the type next selected, null to apply DefaultFilter.
fields.name: savedFilter

fields.description:
BuildID is the content fingerprint of the embedded SPA bundle,
computed by webpack at production build time. Stable across
backend rebuilds that don't touch the bundle, so the SPA can
gate its reload prompt on bundle changes only. Empty for dev
builds where the metadata plugin doesn't run.
fields.name: buildId

fields.description:
Commit is the git sha plus optional `-dirty` marker of the
running portal binary. Useful for diagnostics; not used to gate
the SPA's stale-bundle banner because backend-only rebuilds
would otherwise nag every connected client to reload.
fields.name: commit

fields.description:
TicketConversationMutable reports whether ticket comments can be
edited and deleted, as resolved at startup from
--ticket-comment-mutation-enabled and the declared sync providers.
The ticketsync daemon checks it against its own providers.
fields.name: ticketConversationMutable

fields.description:
Version is the semver tag of the running portal binary
(e.g. "0.1.0"). Stable across hot-reloads of the same build.
fields.name: version

fields.description:
Answered is whether the target returned a response at all. A
target that did not answer is a gap, never a zero.
fields.name: answered

fields.description: ID is the controller or virtual controller id.
fields.name: id

fields.description:
UnavailableReason is a short operator-facing reason when
Answered is false.
fields.name: unavailableReason

fields.description: AnswerExcerpt is the start of the answer's text.
fields.name: answerExcerpt

fields.description:
AssigneeUserID is the single accountable owner working the ticket
to resolution — the support-desk model's one-assignee fix for the
flat assignee set. Setting it is a support action (the resolver
gates SetTicketAssignee on the staff-held ticket:assign verb), and
the manager validates the target is a member of the ticket's org /
site (or a cross-org administrator), the same rule the legacy assign
applied; the target is not itself required to be Mujin staff, so a
non-agent owner is possible and the Zendesk sync degrades it with a
warning. Persisted as the ticket.assignee_user_id column, backfilled
from the collapsed ticket_assignee set (MIN(user_id)). Read-only via
GraphQL; a dedicated set-assignee mutation drives it. AssigneeUserIDs
below stays dual-sourced during the rollout.
fields.name: assigneeUserId

fields.description:
AssigneeUserIDs is a virtual outputonly field populated by the
resolver layer (not stored on the row itself — assignees live
in the ticket_assignee join table). The /ticket list view's
Assignees column reads from here so it doesn't have to issue
a per-row ListTicketAssignees round-trip; ListTickets batches
the fetch via ListTicketAssigneesByTickets. Retained and
dual-sourced alongside the single AssigneeUserID during the
participant-model rollout; dropped by a later cleanup once every
consumer reads the single owner.
fields.name: assigneeUserIds

fields.description:
AuthorUserID is the user who issued CreateTicket. Audit-only;
never used for authz (org membership is the gate). Kept immutable
as a creation fact even after the requester is reassigned — see
RequesterUserID.
fields.name: authorUserId

fields.description:
Cc is the virtual outputonly list of external-facing CC
participants, populated by the resolver layer from ticket_cc
(batched via ListTicketCcByTickets). Each entry is an email and,
for an org-user CC, the linked user id. Not stored on the row.
fields.name: cc

fields.description:
CellID names the cell within SiteID the ticket concerns — RC2
rather than the whole Carlisle floor. Optional, and a narrowing
of the site rather than an alternative to it: the resolver
requires the cell to belong to SiteID, so every site-scoped
access check stays correct without reading this field. A ticket
with no site cannot carry one.
fields.name: cellId

fields.description:
ClosedAt is stamped when CloseTicket lands. Closed is the
terminal state; Reopen is the only path back (lands the row
in open and clears SolvedAt + ClosedAt + ClosedReason +
DuplicateOfTicketID).
fields.name: closedAt

fields.description:
ClosedReason carries the categorical outcome when set:
'resolved' (issue fixed), 'wont_do' (declined), or 'duplicate'
(paired with DuplicateOfTicketID). Nil when a close named no
reason — it is orthogonal to the transition and no longer
defaulted, so a closed ticket may carry no reason.
fields.name: closedReason

fields.description:
CollaboratorUserIDs is the virtual outputonly list of internal
staff collaborators, populated by the resolver layer from the
ticket_collaborator table (batched via
ListTicketCollaboratorsByTickets). Not stored on the row.
fields.name: collaboratorUserIds

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
Description is the initial issue body, stored as markdown. The
frontend exposes both a plaintext editor and a WYSIWYG editor;
both serialize to markdown on write and render from markdown on
read. No HTML is ever stored.
fields.name: description

fields.description:
DuplicateOfTicketID, when non-empty, points at the canonical
ticket this row duplicates. Always paired with ClosedReason ==
TicketClosedReasonDuplicate. The pointer is nulled on canonical
delete (FK ON DELETE SET NULL); the duplicate row stays so the
audit trail survives.
fields.name: duplicateOfTicketId

fields.description:
ExternalStatusLabel preserves the raw status label an external
provider reported (e.g. a Freshdesk custom status "Waiting on 3rd
party"), for display beside the mapped Portal status. Display-only:
it never drives a Portal transition. Nil for portal-native tickets.
See docs/decisions/20260826-support-status-vocabulary.md.
fields.name: externalStatusLabel

fields.description:
IsInternal=true means the whole ticket is support-staff-only —
never shown to the customer org. Settable only by admin-org
callers (gate in tickets/manager.go, mirroring the comment-level
flag); list/count reads served to non-admin-org callers strip
internal tickets entirely (db.TicketOptions.IncludeInternal), and
single-ticket reads are denied by access.CanAccessLoadedTicket,
so a customer-org member never learns the ticket exists. Same
shape and staff-side semantics as TicketComment.IsInternal.
fields.name: isInternal

fields.description:
IsPortalFeedback marks a ticket about Portal itself, opened through
SubmitPortalFeedback: an improvement or a fault in the product, not a
problem at a site. It never carries a site, and ticket sync never
mirrors it to the support desk. Set at creation and never changed.
See docs/decisions/20261106-portal-feedback.md.
fields.name: isPortalFeedback

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
OrganizationID is the owning organization. Required at create
time and immutable thereafter — there is no transfer flow. Same
shape as VirtualController.OrganizationID; admin-org membership
grants visibility across orgs but does not change the bound
owner.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
Priority defaults to TicketPriorityNormal at create time when
the caller leaves it unset. Editable by any org member.
fields.name: priority

fields.description:
Product resolves through the operator-supplied product catalog
(shared with VirtualController) into a license SKU label. Stored
as a string for the same reason as VirtualController.Product —
adding a new product is a deploy change, not a schema change.
fields.name: product

fields.description:
ReleaseIDs is the virtual outputonly list of release ids the
ticket is tagged with — populated by the resolver layer from
the ticket_release join table. Two paths land entries here:
auto-link (a controller / VC with a release_id is attached to
the ticket) and manual pick (a triager picks a release via
AssignTicketRelease). The release detail page's "tickets on
this release" subtable reads the reverse direction via
ListTicketsByRelease.
fields.name: releaseIds

fields.description:
RequesterUserID is the party the ticket is for: the support-desk
requester. Defaults to AuthorUserID at create and is mutable
(reassignable to the actually-affected user under the support-only
reassignment rule in access.CanAccessLoadedTicket). A requester may
be internal (staff) or external (a customer-org user); internal
content stays gated by the viewing surface, not by this role.
Persisted as the ticket.requester_user_id column (unconstrained id,
like AuthorUserID). Read-only via GraphQL for now; dedicated
reassignment mutation lands with the participant-model resolvers.
fields.name: requesterUserId

fields.description:
Sequence is a global monotonic counter assigned at create time
from the singleton `ticket_sequence` row inside the same
transaction as the insert. Globally unique — "#1012" identifies
one ticket portal-wide regardless of site or organization.
The frontend renders it however it wants (e.g. "#1012"); the
backend keeps the schema agnostic so the prefix can change
without a migration.
fields.name: sequence

fields.description:
SiteID is an optional site scope. When set, must belong to
OrganizationID — same-org invariant borrowed from the
controller↔site assignment in db/database_site.go. A non-admin
caller without a matching site membership cannot see the ticket.
fields.name: siteId

fields.description:
SolvedAt is stamped when the ticket enters the solved state (a
reversible resolution). Distinct from ClosedAt: solving does not
close. Cleared on Reopen. The future auto-close automation reads
it to drive solved → closed after a window.
fields.name: solvedAt

fields.description:
Status is the latest lifecycle state. Server-managed: the
tickets domain layer drives transitions, resolvers do not set
it directly except on the create boundary.
fields.name: status

fields.description: Title is the human-readable summary shown in the list view.
fields.name: title

fields.description:
ViewerCapabilities is the set of site-scoped action verbs the
requesting user holds at this ticket's site (e.g.
"ticket:modify"). Computed per request so the client shows an
affordance only to a caller who can act; the resolver re-checks
the verb on every mutation regardless.
fields.name: viewerCapabilities

fields.description: CreatedAt is when the contact was CC'd onto the ticket.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
Email is the contact's address and the CC identity within a ticket.
Stored folded (lower/trimmed), matching user email normalization.
fields.name: email

fields.description: TicketID is the ticket the contact is CC'd onto.
fields.name: ticketId

fields.description:
UserID links the CC to a Portal user when the address belongs to an
existing user in the requester's organization; nil for an
unregistered email-only contact. Only an org-user CC grants
in-Portal ticket read.
fields.name: userId

fields.description:
AuthorUserID is the user who posted the comment. Audit-only;
the per-user-edit gate uses this.
fields.name: authorUserId

fields.description: Body is the comment markdown. Same convention as Ticket.Description.
fields.name: body

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
DeletedAt is the soft-delete marker DestroyComment sets when the
ticket conversation is mutable; reads exclude those rows by
default. On an append-only conversation DestroyComment is refused
and removal is a gated redaction instead.
fields.name: deletedAt

fields.description:
IsInternal=true means support-staff-only — never shown to the
customer org. Settable only by admin-org callers; reads served
to non-admin-org callers strip internal comments entirely.
fields.name: isInternal

fields.description:
IsOriginalRequest marks the first comment that snapshots the
customer's original request at ticket creation.
Set once at create, never through the API. At most one per
ticket: tickets created with a non-empty description get one;
tickets created before this change, or with an empty
description, have none.
fields.name: isOriginalRequest

fields.description:
Timestamp when the row was last modified. Advances on every
edit so frontends can render an "edited" marker by comparing
to CreatedAt.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
OrganizationID denormalizes ticket.organization_id so org-scoped
reads do not need to join. Set at create time, never modified.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
Redaction metadata. Redaction is the only removal path for the
append-only conversation: a platform administrator or Support
Engineer redacts a comment (GDPR/PII), the Body is replaced with a
tombstone, and these record who redacted it, when, and why. All set through the
redaction mutation, never a plain field write — hence outputonly.
RedactedAt is nil until the comment is redacted.
fields.name: redactedAt

fields.description:
TicketID is the parent ticket. Set at create time, never
modified, never null. Indexed at the DB layer because the
thread render is the most common read.
fields.name: ticketId

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
ExternalAuthorEmail is the same author's email where the desk
exposes one (Freshdesk; GitLab notes carry none).
fields.name: externalAuthorEmail

fields.description:
ExternalAuthorName is the author's display name on the external
side, captured on every inbound link so an unresolved desk author
stays auditable in portal. Empty on outbound.
fields.name: externalAuthorName

fields.description:
ExternalID identifies the note/comment within the system —
the note id for GitLab. Unique per system.
fields.name: externalId

fields.description:
IsInbound is true when the content was authored on the
external side and mirrored into the portal, false when a
portal comment was mirrored outwards.
fields.name: isInbound

fields.description: Metadata is the per-system JSONB grab bag, daemon-owned.
fields.name: metadata

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description: OrganizationID denormalizes ticket.organization_id.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description: SyncedAt is when the daemon last reconciled this pair.
fields.name: syncedAt

fields.description:
SyncedBodyHash fingerprints the comment body both sides last
agreed on.
fields.name: syncedBodyHash

fields.description: System names the external system.
fields.name: system

fields.description:
TicketCommentID is the linked comment. Set at create time,
never modified.
fields.name: ticketCommentId

fields.description:
TicketID denormalizes ticket_comment.ticket_id so one
targeted ticket sync loads its whole comment map in one read.
fields.name: ticketId

fields.description:
AuthorUserID is the user who triggered the modify that produced
this revision.
fields.name: authorUserId

fields.description: Body is the markdown body at the time this revision was minted.
fields.name: body

fields.description: CreatedAt is the revision's creation time, immutable.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description: OrganizationID denormalizes the parent comment's owning org.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description: RevisionNumber is the per-comment monotonic counter (1, 2, 3, …).
fields.name: revisionNumber

fields.description: Summary is an optional commit-message style label.
fields.name: summary

fields.description: TicketCommentID is the parent comment. Set at create time, never null.
fields.name: ticketCommentId

fields.description:
ActorUserID is the user who triggered the event. Audit-only,
never null in practice (system-generated events would carry a
reserved id; we don't have any of those today).
fields.name: actorUserId

fields.description:
FromValue is the previous value, when the event records a
transition (status / priority / site / etc.). Empty for
add-only events (assignee added, tag added).
fields.name: fromValue

fields.description: Kind is the discriminator — see TicketEventKind constants.
fields.name: kind

fields.description:
OrganizationID denormalizes the parent ticket's owning org so
per-org reads do not need to join through ticket.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
ReferencedTicketDeleted is set when the ticket a duplicate or link
event names no longer exists; its blanked value then reads as
removed rather than hidden. Not persisted.
fields.name: referencedTicketDeleted

fields.description: TicketID is the parent ticket. Set at create time, never null.
fields.name: ticketId

fields.description:
ToValue is the new value (or the added/removed entity id for
add/remove events). Empty when the event has no payload.
fields.name: toValue

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
ExternalID identifies the mirror within the system — the
issue iid for GitLab ("4385"), the ticket id for Zendesk.
Unique per system.

as a chip on the ticket detail page.

portal core never interprets it.

description) both sides last agreed on — the merge base for
bidirectional content sync.

on, in the external system's vocabulary (GitLab:
opened/closed).

TicketID is the linked ticket. Set at create time, never

rather than the whole Carlisle floor. Optional, and a narrowing

with no site cannot carry one.

frontend exposes both a plaintext editor and a WYSIWYG editor;
both serialize to markdown on write and render from markdown on

inputFields.description:
IsInternal=true means the whole ticket is support-staff-only —
never shown to the customer org. Settable only by admin-org
callers (gate in tickets/manager.go, mirroring the comment-level
flag); list/count reads served to non-admin-org callers strip
internal tickets entirely (db.TicketOptions.IncludeInternal), and
single-ticket reads are denied by access.CanAccessLoadedTicket,
so a customer-org member never learns the ticket exists. Same
shape and staff-side semantics as TicketComment.IsInternal.
inputFields.name: isInternal

inputFields.description:
Priority defaults to TicketPriorityNormal at create time when
the caller leaves it unset. Editable by any org member.
inputFields.name: priority

inputFields.description:
Product resolves through the operator-supplied product catalog
(shared with VirtualController) into a license SKU label. Stored
as a string for the same reason as VirtualController.Product —
adding a new product is a deploy change, not a schema change.
inputFields.name: product

inputFields.description:

RevokedAt is set when the user (or an administrator) explicitly
invalidates the token. The auth path treats a revoked token as
missing; the row is kept around so the settings UI can render
"Revoked <ago>" instead of the entry vanishing under the user
without explanation. Distinct from ExpiresAt so revocation is

CellsUpdated counts the cells re-stamped to the destination org.

Useful for the frontend to invalidate caches that keyed on the
previous owner.

fields.description:
Site is a sub-organization grouping that scopes which controllers a
non-admin org member can see. Sites belong to a single organization;
a controller is in at most one site (which must be in the
controller's own org); a user can join many sites within their
organization. There is no role distinction inside a site for now —
membership is the whole permission.

Visibility is enforced in backend/access:
  - admin-org members see everything
  - per-user org admins see every controller in their own org
  - regular org members see a controller only when both the
    controller has a site AND they are a member of that site

Site mutations and controller<->site assignments require the per-user
org admin flag, mirroring the link/unlink semantics in apigraph/link.go
(admin-org membership is intentionally not special-cased there).

the site (site_id is immutable) and keep their per-site
sequence numbers — the count is purely informational.

scheduler fires it on a recurring or one-shot trigger by appending a
user message to PinnedConversationID and invoking the runner.

See docs/jobs.md (forthcoming) for the multi-instance scheduler
design — claim transitions ride conditional UPDATEs on the row,
mirroring the summarizer-claim pattern already in use elsewhere in
agents/.

Visibility is per-(organization, user); in-org admins do not see
another user's jobs (same rationale as Conversation / memory pages /
ConversationTodo).
fields.name: job

fields.description: IsRemoved is false when the caller had no such registration.

feature is off does not see a control that would fail with a bare
conflict. Global-flag half, so not persisted and empty for other users.

so the frontend can gate the UI on the caller's actual capabilities
rather than a coarse admin check. Computed from the request-scoped snapshot;
empty for users other than the authenticated caller (only the
caller's snapshot is resolved). Not persisted.

fields.description:

whichever SSO broker the user's organization routes through
(WorkOS profile.idp_id, Polis userinfo.id, etc). Set the first

fields.description:

fields.name: action

fields.description:

this mutation was made. Empty on ordinary writes; mirrors
AuditEvent so the feed can flag impersonated actions.

(resolved the same way as AuditEvent), not necessarily the

lands under the customer's org.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:

when the event was written (empty when the model exposes none). The
feed shows it next to the resource type and links it by ResourceID.

fields.description:
ResourceType + ResourceID identify the mutated row. ResourceType
is the shared resource-family enum; ResourceID is the affected

inputFields.description:
Locale is the IETF BCP 47 language tag (e.g. "ja-JP") the user

fields.description:
MFARequired reports that the email factor succeeded but the user
holds passkeys, so no token is issued until the passkey
assertion (BeginPasskeyAssertion / FinishPasskeyAssertion with
this same ticket) completes. The pending page shows the passkey
prompt and keeps polling — if the user's passkeys are deleted
mid-flow (admin recovery), a later poll promotes the session and
returns the token.
fields.name: mfaRequired

fields.description:
RegistrationPending reports that the email factor succeeded on a
self-service sign-up the server requires a platform administrator
to approve. A Token IS issued and the cookie IS set — the browser
holds a real session across a reload — but it resolves to no
principal until the approval provisions the organization and its
first user, so the frontend shows the waiting-for-approval page
instead of the dashboard. UserID is empty.
fields.name: registrationPending

fields.description: Token is the session bearer value (put it in Authorization: Bearer).
fields.name: token

fields.description: ID of the User

(purpose, tenant context, "do not delete" flags, etc.). Editable
by any org member through Modify. Empty string means no comment.

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.

fields.description:
CreatedByUserID is the user who issued CreateVirtualController.
Audit-only; never used for authz (org membership is the gate).
fields.name: createdByUserId

fields.description:
DataUsedBytes is the most recently observed used capacity of the
`/data` PVC, sampled by the reconciler from kubelet stats. Nil
when the VC has never been observed (paused since create, kubelet
unreachable, etc.); the dashboard renders "—" in that case rather
than zero.
fields.name: dataUsedBytes

fields.description:
DestroyedAt is set when Destroy completes. The row is kept for
auditing and to prevent ID reuse rather than hard-deleted.
fields.name: destroyedAt

fields.description:
DiskUsageObservedAt records when the two UsedBytes fields were
last refreshed. Same staleness pattern as StatusObservedAt: the
dashboard renders "—" once this exceeds a UI-side threshold
rather than reporting old numbers as fresh.
fields.name: diskUsageObservedAt

fields.description:
Image is the resolved "registry/repo:tag" reference the
reconciler stamps onto the pod. Output-only — the only writer
is the resolver/manager, which derives it from
ReleaseImageID's release_image row at create and modify time
and re-derives it on every reconcile tick so registry
rewrites flow through without a per-row mutation.

Rows created before the catalog→release switchover (when
release_image_id was nullable on the DB) may carry a literal
image string with ReleaseImageID nil; the reconciler reads
that verbatim until the row is destroyed.
fields.name: image

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
Name is the human-readable label shown in the dashboard. Unique
per organization (enforced at the DB layer).
fields.name: name

fields.description:
OrganizationID is the owning organization. Required at create
time and immutable thereafter — there is no link/unlink flow
like the one Controller has, since portal owns the row from
inception. Membership in an administrator organization grants
visibility across orgs but does not change the bound owner.
fields.name: organizationId

fields.description:
PausedAt is set the first time a Modify(...,paused=true) lands
and cleared on unpause. Distinct from Status="paused" because
pause may take time to converge — PausedAt is the operator's
intent, Status is the cluster's observed state.
fields.name: pausedAt

fields.description:
PrivateUsedBytes mirrors DataUsedBytes for the `/private` PVC.
Tracked separately because the two volumes have different growth
shapes — `/data` is workspace files (bursty), `/private` is logs
and supervisord state (steady).
fields.name: privateUsedBytes

fields.description:
Product resolves through the operator-supplied product catalog
into MUJIN_PRODUCT_ID at /private/mujin_conf.bash render time,
gating which controller features the VC exposes. Stored as a
string for the same reason as Size — adding a new license SKU
is a deploy change, not a schema change.
fields.name: product

fields.description:
Region is the home region for this virtual controller.
Operator-supplied at create time; never hardcoded.
fields.name: region

fields.description:
ReleaseID is the parent release of ReleaseImageID, denormalized
at create / modify time so the frontend can navigate VC →
release in one hop (e.g. the dashboard's per-row release chip)
without joining release_image. Output-only on the GraphQL
surface — the only writers are the create/modify resolvers,
which load it from the chosen release_image's release_id.

Mirrors controller.ReleaseID's contract: SET NULL on release
delete, survives a release_image delete (which only nils
ReleaseImageID).
fields.name: releaseId

fields.description:
ReleaseImageID pins the VC to a row in the portal-global
release_image catalog. The resolver requires it on every new
create — there is no free-form image-string path anymore. The
reconciler reads the linked release_image at apply time and
stamps registry/repo:tag (or registry/repo@digest when the
release_image carries a digest) onto the pod's container image
field, so a registry rewrite on the release_image row flows to
every linked VC on the next tick without a per-row mutation.

Channel-visibility on the parent release is enforced at the
resolver: a caller can only pin a VC to a release_image whose
release is visible to them via access.CanAccessLoadedRelease.

ON DELETE SET NULL on the FK: a release_image hard-delete
nils this column without dropping the row, and the reconciler
falls back to the cached Image string until a future modify
re-pins the VC.
fields.name: releaseImageId

fields.description:
SiteID is the optional Site this VC is assigned to. Mirrors
Controller.SiteID semantics: empty means unassigned (admin-only
within its organization); when set, the site must belong to
the VC's own org (enforced at the DB layer in
AssignVirtualControllerToSite). Output-only on the GraphQL
surface — the only writers are CreateVirtualController (which
accepts an optional siteId on input) and the dedicated
AssignVirtualControllerToSite mutation; ModifyVirtualController
never patches it.
fields.name: siteId

fields.description:
Size resolves through the operator-supplied size catalog into
concrete CPU/memory/disk requests at apply time. Stored as a
string (rather than an enum) so adding a new size is a pure
deploy change — no schema migration, no code edit.
fields.name: size

fields.description:

periodic reconciler from the k8s Deployment status.
fields.name: status

fields.description:
StatusMessage is the most recent error or informational message
from k8s; surfaced verbatim in the UI so an operator can debug
without kubectl access.
fields.name: statusMessage

fields.description:
StatusObservedAt records when Status was last refreshed. The UI
renders a "stale" badge once this exceeds a configured threshold
rather than flipping the row to error when the periodic
reconciler is briefly blocked.
fields.name: statusObservedAt

fields.description:
ViewerCapabilities is the set of site-scoped action verbs the
requesting user holds at this virtual controller's site (e.g.
"virtual_controller:modify"). Computed per request so the client
shows an affordance only to a caller who can act; the resolver
re-checks the verb on every mutation regardless.
fields.name: viewerCapabilities

Channel-visibility on the parent release is enforced at the

"20Gi") parsed into bytes. Each VC has two PVCs at this size,
so the dashboard's total capacity for one VC is 2 *
diskCapacityBytes.

this size, in the plan's currency minor units (e.g. US cents). The

prepaid balance; it is not reported to Stripe.

Comment is a free-text user note: what was just installed, what
is about to be tested, why the user wanted a rollback target.
Optional; empty string is fine.
fields.name: comment

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
CreatedByUserID is the user who issued
CreateVirtualControllerSnapshot. Audit-only; never used for authz
(org membership is the gate, same as VC mutations).
fields.name: createdByUserId

fields.description:
DeletedAt is set when Destroy completes. The row is kept for
auditing rather than hard-deleted.
fields.name: deletedAt

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was last modified.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
OrganizationID denormalizes virtual_controller.organization_id so
org-scoped reads do not need to join. Set at create time, never
modified.

fields.description:
RestoreRequestedAt is stamped when RestoreVirtualControllerSnapshot
flips Status to restoring. Cleared once the reconciler completes
the restore. The dashboard uses this to surface "this snapshot is
being rolled back into the VC right now" without re-reading the
VC's own state.

RestoreSizeBytes is the sum of both VolumeSnapshots' RestoreSize.
Populated by the reconciler once both snapshots report ReadyToUse.
Nil while the snapshot is still pending; the dashboard renders
"—" in that case rather than zero.
fields.name: restoreSizeBytes

fields.description:
SourceImage / SourceSize / SourceProduct freeze the source VC's
catalog selections at snapshot time. A future "fork to new VC"
flow needs these to re-render mujin_conf.bash for the cloned VC;
in-place rollback (the v1 path) does not strictly need them but
they are cheap to record and useful for the dashboard's "this
snapshot is from image X / size Y" badge.
fields.name: sourceImage

fields.description:
Status is the latest observed lifecycle state. The reconciler is
the authority for transitions; resolvers only set the status
directly on the create / restore / destroy boundaries.
fields.name: status

fields.description:

from the reconciler. Surfaced verbatim in the UI so an operator
can debug without kubectl access.
fields.name: statusMessage

fields.description: StatusObservedAt records when Status was last refreshed.
fields.name: statusObservedAt

at create time, never modified, never null. Indexed at the DB
layer because the dashboard's per-VC snapshot list is the most
common read.
fields.name: virtualControllerId

fields.description: IsConfigured reports whether the region and shard appear in the catalogue.
fields.name: isConfigured

fields.description: UnattributedEstimateBytes is the approximate difference between physical shard size and attributed logical rows.
fields.name: unattributedEstimateBytes

fields.description:
Comment is the user-supplied label for the device, e.g.
"MacBook" or "office laptop". Free text, can be edited after
mint. Modifying this bumps ModifiedAt.
fields.name: comment

fields.description: Timestamp when the row was created.
fields.name: createdAt

fields.description:
LastHandshakeAt is the most recent successful WireGuard
handshake observed for this peer. Refreshed by the per-pod
peer-sync loop at most once per reconcile interval; explicitly
excluded from ModifiedAt to keep that field meaningful.
fields.name: lastHandshakeAt

fields.description:
Timestamp when the row was last modified by a user/admin action
(comment rename, revoke). LastHandshakeAt updates do **not**
bump this — that field is high-frequency bookkeeping and would
drown out real changes.
fields.name: modifiedAt

fields.description:
PublicKeyBase64 is the base64-encoded form of PublicKey, populated
by the resolver before output. Surfaced on the GraphQL API as
`publicKey` so the VPN devices page can identify a peer at a
glance — wg admins recognise their devices by pubkey, not by row
id. Output-only; not persisted to the database (gorm:"-").

Declared *before* PublicKey so graphql-go's defaultResolveFn
matches the JSON tag here on its first iteration. If the raw
PublicKey field came first, its case-insensitive Go-name match
against "publicKey" would win and the API would emit the byte
slice instead of the base64 string.
fields.name: publicKey

fields.description:
RevokedAt is set when the device is removed from the user's
"VPN devices" list. The row is kept for audit and to prevent
public-key reuse rather than hard-deleted; the data path
rejects packets from peers whose row has a non-null RevokedAt
within ~30 s (or in-region milliseconds via Redis pub/sub).
fields.name: revokedAt

fields.description:
UserID is the owning user. A peer is bound to a single user;
access decisions for any TCP connection through the tunnel reuse
the existing org-level controller-access check on this user's
organization.
fields.name: userId

types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document. 

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.
types.name: __Directive

types.name: __Schema

types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.
types.name: __Type
